error.idFormat: Use 1 to 40 characters: a-z, 0-9, - and _, starting with a letter or digit.

error.patternsRequired: Pick at least one built-in pattern or write your own.
error.regexEmpty: A pattern must not match empty text.
error.regexInvalid: One of your patterns is not a valid regular expression.
error.regexTooLong: A pattern can be at most 200 characters.
error.regexTooMany: Use at most 5 patterns of your own.
error.timeoutRange: Use a whole number from 100 to 5000.
error.toolGlobFormat: Use letters, digits and _ . : - with * and ? as wildcards (up to 128 characters).
error.urlHttps: Use an https URL, for example https://hooks.example.com/check.

agentLab.capabilitiesLoading: Checking what this workspace can run…
agentLab.capabilitiesUnsupported: This instrument needs a newer server version and is not available here yet.
agentLab.ccCaveat: Agreement is not the same as correctness. Consistent answers can still be wrong.
agentLab.ccContradictionNote: Pairs inside a group that the judge called different from each other: {count}. Each group follows its answers' match with the first answer in the group.
agentLab.ccDetailContradictory: Every answer matched the first one, but the judge also called some of them different from each other (pairs: {count}). The verdicts contradict each other, so run the check again.
agentLab.ccDetailInsufficient: Only {n} of {k} samples finished, which is too few to compare.
agentLab.ccDetailMixed: Answers disagree: {majority} of {n} agree and the rest differ.
agentLab.ccDetailUnstable: Answers disagree: no answer has a majority across {n} samples.
agentLab.ccDetailUnverified: Comparisons without a verdict: {count}. The answers could not be grouped reliably, so run the check again.
agentLab.ccEntropy: Entropy {bits} bits ({percent}% of the maximum for {n} samples)
agentLab.ccEntropyHelp: 0 means every sample landed in one group. Higher means the answers are spread across more groups.
agentLab.ccGroupShowAll: Show all answers in this group
agentLab.ccIncludeHistory: Include the conversation before this turn ({count} messages)
agentLab.ccIntro: Ask the same question several times and see whether the answers mean the same thing.
agentLab.ccMethodNote: Grouped by an LLM judge that compares each pair of answers, running on the same model as the agent.
agentLab.ccNoTurns: No server turns in the playground yet. Type a question instead.
agentLab.ccShareBarLabel: Share of samples in each answer group
agentLab.ccToolsWarning: The original turn used tools. Samples are generated without tools, so they may differ from it for that reason.
agentLab.ccUnknownGroupsNote: Comparisons without a verdict: {count}. The headline is the same whether they count as same or as different, but the groups and the entropy below count them as different ({shown} groups). Counted as same, there would be {alt}.
agentLab.ccUnknownNote: Comparisons without a verdict: {count}. Counting them as same or as different gives the same result.
agentLab.ccZeroTempNote: This agent's temperature is 0, so samples will usually match.
agentLab.estimateOverCap: That is over the limit of {cap} model calls per run. Reduce the selection.
agentLab.estimateUsageNote: Calls count toward your usual usage limits. A run stops after 20 minutes and keeps the results so far.
agentLab.graphCanvasLabel: Run graph for the selected turn
agentLab.graphCompareDetached: The live conversation has moved on from this fork, so only the original is shown.
agentLab.graphCompareNone: No snapshots yet. Fork a turn to keep its original for comparison.
agentLab.graphCompareRemovedTurns: {count} later turns of the original were removed from the live conversation.
agentLab.graphCompareRemovedTurnsOne: 1 later turn of the original was removed from the live conversation.
agentLab.graphCompareSameTools: Both versions called the same tools.
agentLab.graphEmpty: Send a message in the playground to see its run graph here.
agentLab.graphForkAttachmentNote: Attachments from the original message are not sent again.
agentLab.graphForkBody: The conversation is rewound to just before this message, and the message is sent again. Later turns are removed from the live conversation, and the server's running summary of older turns is rebuilt as the conversation continues. The current version is kept as a read-only snapshot so you can compare the two.
agentLab.graphForkBusy: Wait for the current turn to finish before forking.
agentLab.graphForkCacheNote: This agent has response caching turned on. Sending the same message again can return the stored original answer without calling the model, so the branch may be a copy of the original. Edit the message to get a fresh answer. With semantic caching, a lightly edited message can still return a stored answer.
agentLab.graphForkEstimate: This runs 1 agent turn. A turn can make several model calls depending on reasoning depth and tools.
agentLab.graphForkInterleaved: The conversation was rewound, but another turn started before the message could be sent again, so it was not re-sent. The playground transcript no longer matches the server session. The original is kept under Compare. Clear context before continuing this conversation.
agentLab.graphForkMismatch: The server session holds {server} stored messages but this transcript accounts for {local}. Voice calls, a tool approval, a very long conversation or an expired session can cause this. Clear context and try again in a fresh conversation.
agentLab.graphForkNoSession: There is no server session to rewind yet.
agentLab.graphForkOnDevice: This turn was answered on this device and never reached the server session, so it cannot be rewound.
agentLab.graphForkPrefixUnclean: An earlier turn in this conversation failed, was refused, was interrupted or was answered from cache, so the server's stored messages cannot be matched to this transcript. Clear context and try again in a fresh conversation.
agentLab.graphForkResendFailed: The conversation was rewound, but the re-sent message got no reply. Close the lab to see the error in the playground. The original is kept under Compare.
agentLab.graphForkSideEffects: Tool calls the original turn already made are not undone.
agentLab.graphForkSnapshotNotStored: This browser refused to store the snapshot (its storage is full or blocked), so the original would be kept only until this page is reloaded or closed. Nothing has been rewound. Press Rewind and re-run again to go ahead anyway.
agentLab.graphForkTailUnclean: This turn or a later one cannot be rewound because it ran on this device, was refused, was answered from cache, was interrupted, failed or is still running. Forking here is not available.
agentLab.graphForkUnknown: The rewind request failed and the server session could not be confirmed unchanged: {reason} The conversation may have been rewound. The snapshot of the original is kept under Compare. Clear context before continuing this conversation.
agentLab.graphInspectHint: Select a step in the graph to inspect it.
agentLab.graphNoReply: This message has no reply. The send failed or was cancelled before the agent answered.
agentLab.graphNoSteps: This turn reported no intermediate steps. The model answered directly.
agentLab.graphPreviewNote: Arguments and results are shortened previews of up to 400 characters and may be redacted.
agentLab.graphSnapshotNote: Snapshots are kept in this browser only, for 24 hours.
agentLab.koCaveat: Scores come from an LLM judge running on the same model as the agent. Small samples give rough estimates, so treat a label as a lead to check, not a verdict.
agentLab.koChartLabel: Score lost when the section is removed, with the noise floor shaded
agentLab.koDatasetNone: No eval datasets for this agent yet. Use probe questions, or create a dataset on the Quality page.
agentLab.koDatasetNote: Cases with an expected answer are scored against it.
agentLab.koDeltaHelp: Bars show the score lost when the section is removed: a bar to the right means the section helps. The per-question table shows the change itself, the score without the section minus the baseline.
agentLab.koDetailHarmful: Removing it raised the score by {delta}.
agentLab.koDetailLoadBearing: Removing it lowered the score by {delta}.
agentLab.koDetailNoEffect: A change of {delta} is inside the noise floor.
agentLab.koDetailNoFloor: Removing it changed the score by {change}, but there is too little data to tell that apart from noise, so it is not labelled.
agentLab.koDetailNotMeasured: No question produced a usable score for this section.
agentLab.koDetailPending: Removing it has changed the score by {change} so far.
agentLab.koDetailPendingNone: No score for this section yet.
agentLab.koIntro: Remove one section of the system prompt at a time and measure how the score changes on the same questions.
agentLab.koItemTooLong: Question {n} is longer than {max} characters. Shorten it or leave it out.
agentLab.koItemsAgree: {agree} of {total} questions moved the same way.
agentLab.koItemsTrimmed: Only the first {max} questions are used.
agentLab.koLiveNote: The run is still going. The changes measured so far are shown. Labels and the noise floor appear when it finishes.
agentLab.koMeasuredOn: Measured on {items} questions, baseline repeated {repeats} times.
agentLab.koMeasuredOnOne: Measured on 1 question, baseline repeated {repeats} times.
agentLab.koNoBaseline: Not enough baseline scores to estimate the noise floor, so no section can be labelled.
agentLab.koNoPrompt: This agent has no system prompt to split.
agentLab.koNoiseFloorHelp: Estimated from how much the score varied between identical baseline runs, widened for the number of sections tested. A smaller change cannot be told apart from run-to-run variation.
agentLab.koProbesNote: Probe questions have no reference answer, so the judge scores how well each answer addresses the question.
agentLab.koProbesPlaceholder: How do I reset my password?
agentLab.koPromptTooLong: This prompt is longer than {max} characters, which is more than a lab run can send.
agentLab.koRepeatsHint: The unchanged prompt is run this many times to measure the noise floor.
agentLab.koSectionsHint: The prompt is split at headings and blank lines. Untick a section to leave it out of the test.
agentLab.koSectionsMerged: The prompt has more than {max} parts, so the smallest neighbours were merged.
agentLab.koTooFewToLabel: This is too little to tell a real change from noise, so no section could be labelled. Use at least {items} questions, and enough baseline repeats that questions × (repeats − 1) is {df} or more. Add a question or a baseline repeat.

agentTemplates.fileAnalysisUnavailableNote: Attaching data files for analysis is not available for this agent right now - paste the data into the chat instead.
agentTemplates.financeBillsTrackerKnowledgeHint: Pair this with a workflow (see the Workflows page) that emails or WhatsApps you a reminder before a bill's due date.
agentTemplates.financeBillsTrackerTagline: Helps you plan a budget and stay on top of recurring bills.
agentTemplates.fitnessMembershipAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload membership plans, the class schedule, trainer profiles, facility rules and the freeze/cancellation policy.
agentTemplates.fitnessMembershipAssistantTagline: Explains plans, classes and freeze rules, and captures trial and sign-up interest - never a training plan.
agentTemplates.fleetMaintenanceAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload current maintenance logs and service schedules - this agent only works from what you give it, never invents a mileage or date.
agentTemplates.fleetMaintenanceAssistantTagline: Flags overdue service and drafts reminders from your maintenance logs.
agentTemplates.freightQuotationAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the rate card with its version, lane list, service-area map, surcharge schedule and terms.
agentTemplates.freightQuotationAssistantTagline: Explains lane rates, chargeable weight and surcharges, and drafts a quotation summary for your desk.
agentTemplates.gitCommitPrWriterTagline: Turns a diff or summary of changes into a clear commit/PR message.
agentTemplates.healthCompanionTagline: A gentle daily check-in on how someone is feeling and doing.
agentTemplates.homeOrganizerTagline: Breaks decluttering and household projects into small steps.
agentTemplates.homeworkHelperKnowledgeHint: Upload your class notes, textbook chapters, or a syllabus to the Knowledge page so answers match what you're actually being taught.
agentTemplates.homeworkHelperTagline: Explains concepts step by step instead of just giving answers.
agentTemplates.hotelGuestServicesKnowledgeHint: Upload your property guide and local recommendations - connect a reservation tool for live room/booking changes.
agentTemplates.hotelGuestServicesTagline: Answers amenity, policy, and local-recommendation questions for guests.
agentTemplates.hotelPreStayAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload room types, the tariff sheet, amenities, F&B timings, house rules and local-area notes.
agentTemplates.hotelPreStayAssistantTagline: Handles the questions guests actually ask before and during a stay, and routes in-stay requests to the desk.
agentTemplates.hrOnboardingAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your employee handbook, benefits summary, and IT setup guide so this agent answers from your real policies.
agentTemplates.hrOnboardingAssistantTagline: Answers new-hire questions from your handbook and policies.
agentTemplates.incidentTriageAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload past postmortems or runbooks so triage suggestions reflect how your team actually operates.
agentTemplates.incidentTriageAssistantTagline: Helps structure an incident response while it's happening.
agentTemplates.insuranceClaimIntakeAssistantKnowledgeHi: Upload the claims process documents, intimation timelines and document checklists. It records a claim; it never decides one.
agentTemplates.insuranceClaimIntakeAssistantTagline: Takes first-notice-of-loss details and the document checklist, and hands a tidy summary to your claims team.
agentTemplates.insurancePolicyAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload policy wordings, brochures, prospectuses and servicing FAQs. It cannot see a customer's policy record, so everything specific goes to your team.
agentTemplates.insurancePolicyAssistantTagline: Explains cover, exclusions, waiting periods and renewals from your policy wordings, pointing to the clause.
agentTemplates.internalKbQaKnowledgeHint: Upload internal docs, runbooks, or wiki exports - this is the core use case for the Knowledge page.
agentTemplates.internalKbQaTagline: Answers team questions from your internal docs and wikis.
agentTemplates.iso20022PaymentsAnalystKnowledgeHint: Upload scheme rulebooks, cut-off schedules and your repair procedures so it quotes the right section.
agentTemplates.iso20022PaymentsAnalystTagline: Maps MT103 to pacs.008, decodes AC01 and AM04 rejects, and drafts the repair note.
agentTemplates.jewelleryShowroomAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the collection catalogue, making-charge structure, hallmarking policy, exchange/buy-back terms and care instructions. It never quotes a rate.
agentTemplates.jewelleryShowroomAssistantTagline: Explains purity, hallmarking, making charges and buy-back terms, and captures appointment requests.
agentTemplates.jobSearchAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your resume and a few target job descriptions - this agent tailors advice to your actual background, not generic tips.
agentTemplates.jobSearchAssistantTagline: Tailors your resume/cover letters and preps you for interviews.
agentTemplates.languageLearningBuddyTagline: Practices conversation and corrects mistakes gently.
agentTemplates.legacyCodeArchaeologistKnowledgeHint: Upload old tickets, design docs and runbooks; they fill the gaps the code cannot explain.
agentTemplates.legacyCodeArchaeologistTagline: Reconstructs what an undocumented system does and pins it down with characterisation tests.
agentTemplates.legacyPipelineModernizerKnowledgeHint: Upload your release policy, environment list and shared pipeline library so secrets and gates carry over.
agentTemplates.legacyPipelineModernizerTagline: Turns a Jenkinsfile into GitHub Actions or GitLab CI and says which DORA metric each change moves.
agentTemplates.legalDocumentDraftingKnowledgeHint: Upload your firm's templates and precedent documents so drafts match your actual style and terminology.
agentTemplates.legalDocumentDraftingTagline: First-draft letters and memos in your firm's style, for attorney review.
agentTemplates.legalIntakeAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your firm's intake checklist so questions match how your team actually screens matters.
agentTemplates.legalIntakeAssistantTagline: Structures new-client intake questions and summarizes for an attorney - never gives legal advice.
agentTemplates.legalMatterStatusAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload matter notes, cause lists, filing records and your standard update templates. It states nothing the file does not record.
agentTemplates.legalMatterStatusAssistantTagline: Drafts a plain-language client status update from the matter file - for an attorney to review and send.
agentTemplates.linkedinNetworkingCoachKnowledgeHint: Upload your resume so posts and messages reflect your real experience.
agentTemplates.linkedinNetworkingCoachTagline: Drafts posts, connection messages, and your career narrative.
agentTemplates.literatureReviewAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the papers you already have. When this workspace has deep research or web search switched on, it can look further too.
agentTemplates.literatureReviewAssistantTagline: Organises your sources into themes, agreements, conflicts and gaps, with a marker on every claim.
agentTemplates.loanProductExplainerKnowledgeHint: Upload product sheets, rate cards and eligibility criteria. It never asks for an account number, card number, OTP or PIN, and warns customers who offer one.
agentTemplates.loanProductExplainerTagline: Explains eligibility, documents and published rate ranges for an NBFC, branch or DSA - never a sanction.
agentTemplates.logisticsDispatchAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your delivery policies and SLAs - connect a tracking tool for live shipment status.
agentTemplates.logisticsDispatchAssistantTagline: Answers shipment status and delivery-policy questions from your ops docs.
agentTemplates.mainframeAbendTriageKnowledgeHint: Upload batch runbooks, the job dependency chart and cut-off times so rerun advice matches your site.
agentTemplates.mainframeAbendTriageTagline: Reads a failed JCL step and explains S0C7, SB37 or SQLCODE -911 with the fix and the safe rerun.
agentTemplates.mcpAdminOnlyNote: Only a workspace admin can connect a server.
agentTemplates.mcpAllowListWarning: If this agent has a specific list of allowed tools, connecting a server is not enough on its own - open the agent's Tools tab and add the new mcp__ tools to that list, or the agent will not see them.
agentTemplates.mcpCredentialsNeededLabel: Needs a key you create first: {vars}
agentTemplates.mcpNoneLabel: No connection needed - this template works on your own documents.
agentTemplates.mcpOauthLabel: Sign in with the provider (no key to paste)
agentTemplates.mcpOneOfLabel: Pick one of these, not both.
agentTemplates.mcpPlanCapNote: Your plan allows {limit} connected servers in total, from the curated catalogue only. Connecting more than that is refused, so choose before you connect.
agentTemplates.mcpServerAtlassianDescription: Jira issues and Confluence pages. Connects by sign-in, not by a pasted token.
agentTemplates.mcpServerBraveSearchDescription: Live web search, so answers are not limited to training data.
agentTemplates.mcpServerCodeIntelDescription: Call graph and impact analysis over a repository you have indexed.
agentTemplates.mcpServerFilesystemDescription: Reads and writes files in a folder the server can see.
agentTemplates.mcpServerGoogleDriveDescription: Files in Drive. For Gmail, Calendar, Sheets and Drive together, connect Google on the Integrations page instead - that is the supported path.
agentTemplates.mcpServerGoogleMapsDescription: Places, addresses, distances and travel times.
agentTemplates.mcpServerHomeAssistantDescription: Your own Home Assistant instance, for home devices.
agentTemplates.mcpServerMemoryDescription: A scratch knowledge graph the agent can write notes into.
agentTemplates.mcpServerPlaywrightVisionDescription: Opens web pages and can see the rendered screen, not just the text.
agentTemplates.mcpServerPostgresDescription: Queries a database you point it at.
agentTemplates.mcpServerPuppeteerDescription: Opens web pages and reads what is on them.
agentTemplates.mcpServerSapDescription: An SAP system you have credentials for.
agentTemplates.mcpServerSentryDescription: Error reports and stack traces from your projects.
agentTemplates.mcpServerSequentialThinkingDescription: Gives the agent a structured scratchpad for multi-step problems.
agentTemplates.mcpServerSlackDescription: Reads and posts in the channels you allow.
agentTemplates.mcpServerSqliteDescription: Queries a SQLite file on the server.
agentTemplates.mealPlannerTagline: Plans meals around what you have and what you like.
agentTemplates.meetingNotesSummarizerTagline: Turns raw notes or a transcript into a clear action-item list.
agentTemplates.monolithDecompositionStrategistKnowledge: Upload the ERD, module list, architecture docs and incident history; it cites them when ranking options.
agentTemplates.monolithDecompositionStrategistTagline: Finds the first slice to carve out and plans the strangler-fig path, data moves and rollback.
agentTemplates.multilingualSupportAgentKnowledgeHint: Upload your FAQ or product docs so answers stay grounded in what you actually offer. To let this agent translate, transcribe voice notes, and reply with spoken audio in Indian languages, activate a Sarvam AI key on the Providers page first - without it, this agent still works, just in whatever language the conversation is already in.
agentTemplates.multilingualSupportAgentTagline: Supports customers in Hindi, Tamil, and other Indian languages.
agentTemplates.ngoGrantReportWriterKnowledgeHint: Upload programme documents, monitoring data, past reports and the funder's guidelines. Missing figures become marked placeholders, never estimates.
agentTemplates.ngoGrantReportWriterTagline: Drafts funder reports to their own structure, with every number traced to a document you uploaded.
agentTemplates.notesToRevisionKitKnowledgeHint: Upload your class notes to the Knowledge page, or paste them into the chat - everything is built from them, and anything not in your notes is labelled.
agentTemplates.notesToRevisionKitTagline: Turns your own notes into a summary, flashcards, a revision plan and a mock test.
agentTemplates.patientIntakeAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your intake forms, insurance, and billing policy documents.
agentTemplates.patientIntakeAssistantTagline: Walks patients through forms, insurance, and check-in - never gives medical advice.
agentTemplates.pharmacyCounterAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the catalogue with pack sizes and MRP, delivery areas and charges, and the prescription policy.
agentTemplates.pharmacyCounterAssistantTagline: Handles timings, delivery, stock listings and refill requests - never a dose, substitute or side effect.
agentTemplates.prePrReviewBuddyTagline: Reviews a pasted diff for bugs, risks and missing tests before a teammate sees it.
agentTemplates.productListingCopyWriterKnowledgeHint: Upload spec sheets, labels and existing catalogue entries. A missing attribute is written as MISSING, never invented.
agentTemplates.productListingCopyWriterTagline: Writes marketplace titles, bullets and attributes from the spec sheet - marking anything it cannot evidence.
agentTemplates.productionSopAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload SOPs, work instructions, machine manuals and quality checklists. Without them it has no procedure to quote, and it will say so rather than improvise.
agentTemplates.productionSopAssistantTagline: Answers shop-floor and quality questions from your SOPs and work instructions, citing the step it read.
agentTemplates.projectManagerAssistantTagline: Helps break down projects and track what's blocking what.
agentTemplates.projectSalesEnquiryAssistantKnowledgeHin: Upload the RERA registration, approved floor plans and carpet areas, price list, payment schedule and specifications.
agentTemplates.projectSalesEnquiryAssistantTagline: Answers buyers on floor plans, payment schedule, RERA details and possession - only from approved documents.
agentTemplates.propertyListingAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your current listing sheets - price, layout, and availability answers only ever come from what you upload here.
agentTemplates.propertyListingAssistantTagline: Answers listing questions from your sheets and captures buyer/renter details.
agentTemplates.proposalInvoiceDrafterKnowledgeHint: Upload an old proposal or your rate card so drafts follow your own wording and terms.
agentTemplates.proposalInvoiceDrafterTagline: Drafts client proposals with a clear scope, and invoices with the arithmetic shown.
agentTemplates.realEstateLeadFollowUpKnowledgeHint: Upload current listings so suggested properties come from real inventory, not a guess.
agentTemplates.realEstateLeadFollowUpTagline: Drafts warm, specific follow-ups based on what a lead told you they need.
agentTemplates.relatedDailyBriefingLink: Run it every morning with the Daily Briefing workflow template
agentTemplates.relatedTutorLink: Want a full course instead? Open the Tutor
agentTemplates.relatedWhatsappApprovalLink: Want replies sent after you approve them? See the workflow template
agentTemplates.rentalTenantSupportAssistantKnowledgeHin: Upload tenancy agreements, house rules, society bye-laws, maintenance SOPs and the escalation matrix.
agentTemplates.rentalTenantSupportAssistantTagline: Answers tenants and owners from the agreement itself and routes maintenance complaints by your escalation matrix.
agentTemplates.researchAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the articles, papers, or notes you're researching - answers stay grounded in what you actually gave it.
agentTemplates.researchAssistantTagline: Helps you understand and organize a topic you're digging into.
agentTemplates.restaurantReservationAssistantKnowledgeH: Upload your menu, allergen info, and reservation policies - connect a booking tool for live table availability.
agentTemplates.restaurantReservationAssistantTagline: Answers menu, hours, and dietary questions; routes bookings to your team.
agentTemplates.resumeCoverLetterTailorKnowledgeHint: Upload your resume and projects to the Knowledge page, then paste the job description into the chat.
agentTemplates.resumeCoverLetterTailorTagline: Fits your resume bullets and a short cover letter to one job, without inventing experience.
agentTemplates.retailOffersFaqAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload offer circulars with validity windows, the loyalty programme terms, and the exchange/refund policy.
agentTemplates.retailOffersFaqAssistantTagline: Answers shoppers on live offers, loyalty, exchange and refund policy with the validity window attached.
agentTemplates.rfqQuotationAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload product specifications, datasheets, your standard rate card, MOQ and payment terms - it quotes only what these documents say.
agentTemplates.rfqQuotationAssistantTagline: Turns a buyer enquiry into a priced-up draft quotation from your own specs, rate card and terms.
agentTemplates.salesLeadQualifierKnowledgeHint: Upload your product one-pager and ideal-customer profile so questions stay relevant to what you actually sell.
agentTemplates.salesLeadQualifierTagline: Asks the right questions to size up an inbound lead.
agentTemplates.salesSheetAnalystTagline: Works out the numbers in your sales or expense sheet by running code, not by guessing.
agentTemplates.salonBookingAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the service menu with prices and durations, stylist or therapist specialisations, and product/aftercare notes.
agentTemplates.salonBookingAssistantTagline: Shares services, prices and stylist availability and captures appointment requests for the desk to confirm.
agentTemplates.schoolOfficeAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the prospectus, fee structure, admission notices, academic calendar and transport routes. It never discusses an individual student.
agentTemplates.schoolOfficeAssistantTagline: Answers parents on admissions, fees, timings and circulars in their own language, and logs enquiries.
agentTemplates.setupStepChannelBody: A customer-facing agent that only lives in this console has not really shipped. Connect WhatsApp, Telegram or email on the Channels page and point the channel at this agent.
agentTemplates.setupStepChannelTitle: 2. Put it where your customers are
agentTemplates.setupStepKnowledgeBody: This template answers from your files, not from general knowledge - with an empty collection it is worse than a plain chat. Create a collection and upload the documents listed above. The Free plan includes one collection.
agentTemplates.setupStepMcpBody: Open the Tools page and connect the servers listed above. Some activate in one click; the rest need a key or a sign-in first. Only a workspace admin can do this.
agentTemplates.setupStepProviderBody: Model, code-execution and voice keys live on the Providers page. Store a key once there and refer to it from the agent; never paste a key into a chat.
agentTemplates.setupStepToolAccessBody: Open the agent's Tools tab and tick the new tools. If the agent has a specific allowed-tools list, a newly connected server stays invisible to it until you add the tools there.
agentTemplates.socialMediaContentKnowledgeHint: Upload brand voice guidelines or past posts so drafts actually sound like your organization.
agentTemplates.socialMediaContentTagline: Drafts on-brand posts and captions for review before you post.
agentTemplates.technicalDocsWriterKnowledgeHint: Upload existing docs or code comments so new documentation matches your project's real structure.
agentTemplates.technicalDocsWriterTagline: Drafts API docs, READMEs, and runbooks from what you describe.
agentTemplates.testCaseGeneratorTagline: Suggests test cases and edge cases for a feature or function.
agentTemplates.textileBuyerEnquiryAssistantKnowledgeHin: Upload the product catalogue, fabric specification sheets, shade cards and trade terms. Specifications are repeated exactly, never paraphrased.
agentTemplates.textileBuyerEnquiryAssistantTagline: Answers buyers on composition, GSM, shades, MOQ and lead time, and logs swatch and sample requests.
agentTemplates.tourPackageAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload package itineraries, inclusions and exclusions, tariff sheets, visa document checklists and the cancellation policy.
agentTemplates.tourPackageAssistantTagline: Walks travellers through itineraries, inclusions, exclusions and visa checklists from your own tariff sheets.
agentTemplates.travelPlannerKnowledgeHint: You do not have live flight, hotel, or pricing data unless a booking tool is connected - treat suggestions as a starting point to verify yourself.
agentTemplates.travelPlannerTagline: Builds itineraries and packing lists around your trip.
agentTemplates.vehicleShowroomAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload brochures, variant and price lists, accessory lists and the published finance illustration sheet.
agentTemplates.vehicleShowroomAssistantTagline: Compares variants, explains on-road breakup and finance illustrations, and captures test-drive requests.
agentTemplates.vendorBoqAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload the tender documents, BOQ, specifications and the vendor quotations you are comparing. It flags omissions rather than filling them.
agentTemplates.vendorBoqAssistantTagline: Reads tender documents and BOQs and lays vendor quotations side by side on the lines they share.
agentTemplates.whatsappBookingAssistantKnowledgeHint: Upload your services, durations and prices so it can answer booking questions.
agentTemplates.whatsappBookingAssistantTagline: Collects appointment requests on WhatsApp and hands them to your team to confirm.
agentTemplates.whatsappFrontDeskKnowledgeHint: Upload your hours, services, prices and policies. It answers only from them.
agentTemplates.whatsappFrontDeskTagline: Answers questions about your business on WhatsApp from your own documents, hands off the rest.
agentTemplates.whatsappLeadFollowupKnowledgeHint: Upload your product or service details so it can answer enquiry questions.
agentTemplates.whatsappLeadFollowupTagline: Follows up on enquiries, collects what sales needs and hands over a qualified lead.
agentTemplates.whatsappPaymentFollowupTagline: Polite invoice reminders and replies about one payment, with disputes passed to a person.
agentTemplates.whatsappReplyDrafterKnowledgeHint: Upload your price list, policies and FAQs so drafts quote your real answers. Do not connect this agent to a channel - a channel would send its replies for you.
agentTemplates.whatsappReplyDrafterTagline: Drafts replies for you to copy and send. It never sends anything itself.
agentTemplates.writingEditorTagline: Tightens up emails, essays, or any draft you paste in.

agentTemplatesPage.introPrefix: Pick a starting point - each one only pre-fills the create form on the
agentTemplatesPage.introSuffix: , nothing is created until you name it and submit there.
agentTemplatesPage.title: Agent Templates

agentTrifecta.advice: Remove one of the three, or make a person approve what it sends.
agentTrifecta.approvalAlreadyOn: Approval is already required for every tool call.
agentTrifecta.blockedNote: Changes that add to this tool mix are rejected.
agentTrifecta.body: It can read private data, take in content written by outsiders, and send data out. Instructions hidden in that outside content could make it send the private data away.
agentTrifecta.enforcedNote: Your workspace requires approval for agents with this tool mix, so this agent now waits for a person before every action.
agentTrifecta.gatedNote: Actions that send data out now always need your approval for this agent.
agentTrifecta.requireApproval: Require approval for every tool call
agentTrifecta.saveBlockedTitle: That tool change was not saved
agentTrifecta.title: Risky tool mix: this agent could leak private data
agentTrifecta.unclassifiedMany: {count} tools could not be judged for this check.
agentTrifecta.unclassifiedOne: 1 tool could not be judged for this check.

agentVersionsCard.emptyVersions: No saved versions yet. One is recorded the first time this agent's configuration is saved.
agentVersionsCard.explainer: A snapshot is saved automatically every time this agent's configuration changes. Labels mark the version you consider good - "Restore" is the action that actually rolls the agent back (and is itself recorded, so it can be undone).
agentVersionsCard.forceReasonLabel: Override reason (required, written to the audit log)
agentVersionsCard.forceReasonPlaceholder: Why is this safe to promote without a passing eval?
agentVersionsCard.markStagingTooltip: Point the staging label at this version.
agentVersionsCard.promoteTooltip: Point the production label at this version. If a promotion gate is configured it may require a passing eval run first.
agentVersionsCard.restoreConfirmBody: The agent's current configuration is replaced by this version's. The restore itself is saved as a new version, so it can be undone.
agentVersionsCard.restoreTooltip: Make this version the agent's current configuration.
agentVersionsCard.restoredNotice: Restored - the agent now runs this configuration.

agentWorkbench.agentDuplicatedSuccess: Duplicated as "{name}" - the copy is freshly editable.
agentWorkbench.agentLimitBanner: You've used all {limit} agents included in your plan. Upgrade to create more.
agentWorkbench.agentLimitReached: You've reached your plan's limit of {limit} agents.
agentWorkbench.agentSystemPromptExamplePlaceholder: e.g. a support agent that handles refunds and order status, friendly but concise
agentWorkbench.autonomyQueueNote: Approval requests land in the workspace's approvals queue, and a tool call that is waiting is not run - the agent is told so and carries on with the rest of the turn.
agentWorkbench.autonomyTierFULLY_AUTONOMOUSCost: Never asks you: every tool call runs as soon as the agent makes it, sends and payments included.
agentWorkbench.autonomyTierFULLY_AUTONOMOUSHint: Never waits for approval, and gets a higher step ceiling. It will act without asking.
agentWorkbench.autonomyTierSEMI_AUTONOMOUSCost: Asks you only for the actions your workspace's approval rules name; the rest run without asking.
agentWorkbench.autonomyTierSEMI_AUTONOMOUSHint: Follows the workspace's approval policy for each action type. The default for every agent.
agentWorkbench.autonomyTierSUPERVISEDCost: Asks you before every tool call, searches included.
agentWorkbench.autonomyTierSUPERVISEDHint: Every tool call waits for a human to approve it, whatever the workspace policy says. Tighter step ceiling.
agentWorkbench.blockedServersCheckFailed: Couldn't check for blocked servers - some unavailable tools may not be explained above.
agentWorkbench.byokModelFreeText: Type any model id, or pick one from the list.
agentWorkbench.capabilitiesDraftHint: Save this agent first to attach capabilities.
agentWorkbench.capabilitiesEmpty: No capabilities are available for this agent.
agentWorkbench.capabilitiesExplainer: Optional tools and integrations this agent can use. The list and its availability come from the platform - entries marked Needs setup just need their credential configured on the Providers page.
agentWorkbench.capabilityToggleError: Couldn't update that capability. Please try again.
agentWorkbench.changeModelFreePlanTooltip: Premium unlocks any provider + your own key. Free-plan agents run on the platform-hosted model.
agentWorkbench.changeModelOnLocalModelTooltip: Your agents run on the local model (Ollama), so changing the model here won't affect what they use. Change the local model under Providers or on Troubleshoot, or switch to your own provider.
agentWorkbench.changeModelOnPlatformLlmTooltip: Your agent is on the managed Platform LLM pool, so changing the model here won't affect what it actually uses. Switch back to your own provider (BYOK) to pick a model.
agentWorkbench.clearCostRoutingError: Could not clear this agent's cost routing.
agentWorkbench.clearFallbackError: Could not clear this agent's fallback provider.
agentWorkbench.codeIntelCheckFailedBanner: Couldn't check whether code intelligence is available - this may not reflect the actual status.
agentWorkbench.codeIntelReadOnlyHint: Read-only code search and navigation tools are always available to agents — no setup needed.
agentWorkbench.codeIntelToolsHint: Per-tool on/off for search, graph navigation and the analysis suite (repo map, references, implementations, call paths, dead code, API surface, hotspots) lives in the Tools section.
agentWorkbench.codeIntelUnavailableBanner: The code intelligence service isn't available right now. Workspace tools stay disabled until it's reachable.
agentWorkbench.codeWorkspaceDraftHint: Save this agent first to enable code-workspace tools and grant repository access.
agentWorkbench.codeWorkspaceEnableHint: Enable workspace tools under Capabilities above to let this agent write and run code in the repositories you grant.
agentWorkbench.codeWorkspaceExplainer: Enable workspace tools to let this agent make and run changes in the repositories you explicitly grant it access to.
agentWorkbench.costRoutingFreePlanTooltip: Cost routing is available on paid plans. Free-tier agents always run on the platform-hosted model.
agentWorkbench.costRoutingOnPlatformLlmTooltip: Cost routing has no effect while this tenant is on the managed Platform LLM pool - routing only applies once you switch to your own provider (BYOK).
agentWorkbench.costRoutingSetSuccess: Cost routing set to {provider} · {model} - simple turns may now route here instead of the primary model.
agentWorkbench.costRoutingTooltip: Route simple turns to a cheaper economy model instead of this agent's primary model
agentWorkbench.deleteAgentError: Could not delete this agent - it may still be connected to a channel.
agentWorkbench.deleteAgentFreePlanTooltip: Deleting agents is a paid-plan feature.
agentWorkbench.denyAllRepoHint: Leave all unchecked to deny this agent access to every repository.
agentWorkbench.draftHint: Draft - fill in the fields below, then Save draft to create it.
agentWorkbench.edgeDetailsScopeNote: This browser session only - resets on reload, not a server-side record.
agentWorkbench.edgeErrorCountNote: {count} on-device turn(s) errored outright this session.
agentWorkbench.editLockBannerText: This agent's 24-hour Free-plan edit window has ended - it keeps running, chatting and answering as-is. Duplicate it for a fresh editable copy, or upgrade to edit it directly.
agentWorkbench.editLockedTooltip: Editing is a Premium feature - duplicate this agent to make changes
agentWorkbench.fallbackClearedSuccess: Fallback cleared - a provider failure will surface directly again.
agentWorkbench.fallbackFreePlanTooltip: Fallback providers are available on paid plans. Free-tier agents always run on the platform-hosted model.
agentWorkbench.fallbackOnPlatformLlmTooltip: Fallback providers have no effect while this tenant is on the managed Platform LLM pool - fallback only applies once you switch to your own provider (BYOK).
agentWorkbench.fallbackSetSuccess: Fallback set to {provider} · {model} - future outages on the primary provider now retry here automatically.
agentWorkbench.fallbackTooltip: Automatically retry on a second provider/model if the primary one fails
agentWorkbench.healthChipNotScoredTitle: The hourly health check has not scored this agent yet. It appears here after the next run.
agentWorkbench.healthChipTitle: Health score {score}/100 - {issues} open issues, {suggestions} pending suggestions. Last checked: {when}.
agentWorkbench.jevThresholdTooltip: How sure the active decision provider must be that a turn is simple before routing it to the economy model — 0.5–0.99. Blank inherits the workspace policy (Decision providers page) or the platform default.
agentWorkbench.knowledgeWriteLabel: Allow writing to the knowledge base (add_to_knowledge_base tool)
agentWorkbench.knowledgeWriteLoadError: Could not load this agent's knowledge-write settings.
agentWorkbench.loadingReposError: Couldn't load repositories. Please try again.
agentWorkbench.localModelNote: This agent runs on the local model {model} through Ollama on this machine. The provider and model picked here are ignored while the local model is on; change the model under Providers, Set up a local model, or on Troubleshoot.
agentWorkbench.localModelNoteUnavailable: This agent runs on the local model (Ollama) on this machine. The active model is not being reported right now.
agentWorkbench.maxTokensThinkingHint: On Gemini 2.5 models, internal thinking shares this max-tokens budget — values below ~2048 can cut replies short.
agentWorkbench.modelCatalogLoadError: Couldn't load the model list — enter a model id manually.

agentsGuide.step1Body: Write a system prompt that tells the agent who it is, its tone, and what it should (and shouldn't) do.
agentsGuide.step2Body: Choose the AI model that powers it. Stay on Simple for smart defaults, or switch to Manual to tune temperature, tokens, fallback and cost routing.
agentsGuide.step3Body: Attach knowledge collections so the agent answers from your own documents — with citations — instead of guessing.
agentsGuide.step4Body: Turn on tools and MCP connectors so the agent can take real actions: look things up, call services, and complete tasks end to end.
agentsGuide.step5Body: Chat with the agent live on the right to see exactly how it responds — and which tools it used — before anyone else does.
agentsGuide.step6Body: Happy with it? Deploy the agent to WhatsApp, the web widget, or any other channel and it goes live for your customers.
agentsGuide.subtitle: An agent is an AI assistant you shape in six quick steps. Here's the whole flow.

approvalsQueue.rulesNeverRiskyWarn: This tool looks like it changes things. Be sure.
approvalsQueue.rulesSavedNever: {tool} will no longer ask for approval.

approvalsQueue.rulesToolNameInvalid: A tool name has no spaces.
approvalsQueue.selectAllLabel: Select all pending tool calls on this page
approvalsQueue.tierFullConsequence: It acts without asking. Only use it for agents whose mistakes are cheap to undo.
approvalsQueue.tierFullWhat: No tool call ever waits for approval and the agent gets a higher limit on tool steps. Per-tool rules are ignored.
approvalsQueue.tierSemiConsequence: A good default. Your per-tool rules take effect here.
approvalsQueue.tierSemiWhat: The workspace's rule for each tool decides: risky tools such as sending, deleting and payments ask by default, the rest run.
approvalsQueue.tierSupervisedConsequence: Safest, but expect a lot of requests in the queue and a slower agent.
approvalsQueue.tierSupervisedWhat: Every tool call waits for a person, whatever the workspace rules say. It also gets a lower limit on tool steps per turn.
approvalsQueue.tiersIntro: Each agent has an autonomy level. It decides whether the workspace's approval rules are used at all.
approvalsQueue.tiersRuleNote: Tool rules (Always ask, Never ask) only matter for Semi-autonomous agents.
approvalsQueue.tiersTitle: Who decides what waits for approval?
approvalsQueue.whyGated: The agent asked to use {tool}. It was held for your decision because the agent is set to Supervised, or because this workspace requires approval for that tool.

evalControls.autoApproveConfirmBody: Every tool call in this dataset's replays that would wait for a person will be approved automatically. Approved tools that only read run for real; approved tools that could change something are still simulated. Only do this in a workspace with test data. Runs record that they were auto-approved.
evalControls.autoApproveHelp: A tool call that would normally wait for a person is approved by the eval sandbox, so the case can finish. Without this the case ends at the unanswered approval, as it would in production.
evalControls.autoApproveLabel: Auto-approve tool calls in the eval sandbox
evalControls.autoApproveNeedsFull: Switch on the full pipeline first: auto-approval only applies when tools run.
evalControls.autoApproveWarnBody: Never turn this on where tools reach real customers or data. Shell, coding, scheduling, agent-to-agent, payment and delete tools are never auto-approved. Your administrator must have marked this workspace as non-production.
evalControls.datasetModeDefaultTitle: This dataset follows the workspace default for how runs replay.
evalControls.datasetModePinnedTitle: This dataset always replays this way. A single run can still choose another mode.
evalControls.modeDefaultHelp: Follows your workspace's setting (the full pipeline unless an admin changed it). Each run can still choose its own mode.
evalControls.modeFullHelp: The same tools, guardrails and step limits a live user gets. Needed for expected-tool and trajectory checks.
evalControls.modeFullNote: Tools that only read run for real. Anything that could change data, send a message or spend money is simulated and listed in the run, so nothing real happens. Tools without a safety classification are simulated too.
evalControls.modeHelp: Choose whether a replay may use the agent's tools. This changes what the next run measures.
evalControls.modeTextOnlyHelp: The agent answers without its tools. Safe: nothing real happens. Expected-tool checks cannot be met.
evalControls.runAutoApprovedTitle: A person decided none of this run's tool calls; the eval sandbox approved them.
evalControls.runModeFullTitle: This run used the full pipeline in the eval sandbox.
evalControls.runModeHelp: Full pipeline runs the agent with its tools, guardrails and approvals in a safe sandbox: tools that only read really run, anything that could change data or send something is simulated. Quick withholds the tools and tests the written answer only.
evalControls.runModeLabel: Replay mode for the next run
evalControls.runModeQuickTitle: This run was a quick text-only replay: the agent's tools were withheld.
evalControls.runSimulatedTools: Simulated, not executed in this run (they could change data or reach outside the platform): {tools}.
evalControls.samplingHelp: A lower rate costs less and means fewer scores in the trend above. This value is read-only here.
evalControls.samplingUnavailable: The share of live turns scored by the background judge is set by your platform administrator and is not shown here.
evalControls.samplingValue: About {percent}% of live turns are scored by the background quality judge.
evalControls.saveFailed: Could not save the replay mode.
evalControls.trajectoryHelpOff: Trajectory checks are not available here. They are switched on for the whole deployment by your administrator, and need a plan that includes evals.
evalControls.trajectoryHelpOn: Cases with an expected trajectory are scored on which tools the agent called and in what order. This is switched on for the whole deployment by your administrator, not per dataset.
evalControls.trajectoryNeedsFull: This dataset is text only, so cases with an expected trajectory will not be scored. Switch on the full pipeline.

explainersAgents.hookAfterBlockBody: the model is told the result was withheld, and why
explainersAgents.hookAfterBody: They see the result before the model does. A hook can also add a short note after it.
explainersAgents.hookAfterRedactBody: matching text is removed from the result before the model reads it
explainersAgents.hookAllowBody: no hook objects, so the call goes ahead
explainersAgents.hookApprovalBody: the call waits in the approvals queue and does not run until a person approves it
explainersAgents.hookAskBody: It names the tool and the arguments it wants to pass.
explainersAgents.hookAskTitle: The model asks to use a tool
explainersAgents.hookBeforeBody: Only enabled hooks that match this tool take part. A webhook hook can also allow or refuse the call, and a log hook only records it.
explainersAgents.hookBlockBody: the call is not run, because a hook blocks it or its rate limit is used up, and the agent is told why
explainersAgents.hookIntro: What happens each time this agent wants to use a tool. Hooks run in the order listed, workspace defaults first.
explainersAgents.hookRecordBody: Blocks, approvals, redactions and hook failures are written to the audit log as agent.hook.decision.
explainersAgents.hookRedactBody: matching text is removed from the arguments first; if that cannot be done safely, the call is not run
explainersAgents.hookRunBody: With the arguments that passed the checks.
explainersAgents.policyAllowedBody: every rule passes, so the call moves on to the usual approval and safety checks
explainersAgents.policyAskBody: It names the tool and the arguments it wants to pass.
explainersAgents.policyAskTitle: The model asks to use a tool
explainersAgents.policyCheckBody: Each rule looks at one argument. This happens before any approval step. A tool with no policy is not checked here.
explainersAgents.policyCheckTitle: The arguments are checked against the policy
explainersAgents.policyDeniedBody: the tool is not run. The agent is told which argument broke which rule, never the value, and can correct it and try again
explainersAgents.policyIntro: What happens when this agent calls a tool that has a policy here.
explainersAgents.policyRecordBody: It appears in the audit log as tool.arg_policy.denied. Argument values are never written to the log.

explainersWorkflow.errorDecideTitle: Still failing: "When this node fails" decides
explainersWorkflow.errorFailsBody: It throws an error or reports a failure.
explainersWorkflow.errorIntro: What happens when this node fails. These settings only take effect when this deployment has the node error strategy switched on.
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeBranchBody: the run goes to whatever the red port is wired to. With nothing wired, the run ends as failed.
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeBranchLabel: Follow the red error port if one is connected, otherwise stop
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeContinueBody: the run follows the node's normal path, and the next node receives the error message and this node's id. A plan limit or a validation problem still stops the run.
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeContinueLabel: Continue, passing the error on as this node's output
explainersWorkflow.errorOutcomeStopBody: the run ends as failed. If the red error port is connected, the failure goes there instead.
explainersWorkflow.errorRetryBody: Up to the total attempts you set, pausing between attempts. A node that can send or change something outside the workflow is not retried unless you allow it.
explainersWorkflow.errorRetryTitle: If retry is on, it is tried again first
explainersWorkflow.switchArriveBody: Each case reads its fields from the incoming data.
explainersWorkflow.switchOutcomeDefaultBody: the run leaves through the Default port.
explainersWorkflow.switchOutcomeMatchBody: the run leaves through the port named after that case. Later cases are not checked, even if they would match too.
explainersWorkflow.switchPassBody: The next node receives exactly what the Switch received.
explainersWorkflow.switchTestBody: A case with no name or no conditions is skipped.
explainersWorkflow.switchTestTitle: Cases are tested from top to bottom
explainersWorkflow.waitIntro: A Wait node pauses a run without keeping anything running.
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeCallBody: a POST to the run's private resume link continues the run.
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutContinueBody: the run carries on down the same path. There is no separate timeout branch.
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutContinueLabel: Nothing arrives in time: Continue the run
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutFailBody: the run ends as failed. This is the default.
explainersWorkflow.waitOutcomeTimeoutFailLabel: Nothing arrives in time: Fail the run
explainersWorkflow.waitParkedBody: The pause is stored, so it survives restarts. While the run is parked no step runs and no model is called.
explainersWorkflow.waitReachBody: The time or date is worked out now, including any expressions. A time that has already passed, or a wait of zero, does not pause at all. Test runs that simulate sends skip the wait.
explainersWorkflow.waitReachTitle: The run reaches the Wait node
explainersWorkflow.waitResumeCallBody: The next node receives the posted JSON as "resume" next to the original "input". After a timeout that continues, it receives "timedOut": true instead of "resume".
explainersWorkflow.waitResumeTimeBody: The next node receives exactly what the Wait node received.
explainersWorkflow.waitResumeTitle: The run continues at the next node
explainersWorkflow.waitWakeCallTitle: A call arrives, or the wait gives up
explainersWorkflow.waitWakeTimeBody: A scheduled sweep wakes the run at or shortly after the time, usually within about a minute.

helpPage.adminPara1: Users: invite teammates and assign roles (only a tenant-admin can change roles or credentials). Approvals is the human-in-the-loop inbox - any action your guardrail policy flags as needing sign-off (e.g. an agent about to send a WhatsApp message) waits here until approved or rejected. Audit Log is a complete, append-only record of every significant action taken in your tenant, by a person or an agent.
helpPage.agentsPara1: An agent is one AI persona: a system prompt, an LLM provider/model, and optionally a knowledge base and a restricted set of tools. Start from a template (support triage, research assistant, etc.) to pre-fill a reasonable system prompt, or start from scratch and use Ask AI to draft one.
helpPage.agentsPara2: Tool access and knowledge access are both allow-lists: leave them empty for "unrestricted" (the agent can use anything currently available to your tenant), or check specific items to restrict the agent to only those. This matters for anything customer-facing - you generally don't want a public support bot to have access to every internal tool.
helpPage.askAiPara1: Any field asking for a system prompt or description - an agent's system prompt, a knowledge collection's description, and more over time - has a small ✨ Ask AI button next to its label. Click it, describe what you want in a sentence (e.g. "a support agent that handles refunds and order status"), and it drafts the text using whichever LLM provider you've already activated. Nothing is applied automatically - you always review the suggestion and click Use this yourself, or Regenerate for another try.
helpPage.channelsPara1: Under Admin → Channels: connect WhatsApp either through Twilio (fast sandbox setup, small per-message fee) or directly through Meta's own WhatsApp Business Platform (no middleman fee, more setup - your own Meta App, System User token, and App Secret). If both are configured, the direct Meta connection is used automatically.
helpPage.channelsPara2: The first time a new phone number messages in, it shows up under Pending sender pairings and needs to be approved before your agents will hold a live conversation with it - this stops a stranger messaging your number from getting an unattended AI conversation by default.
helpPage.devicesPara1: Pair a phone (Android or iOS) to your tenant from the Devices page, and a workflow's Device Control node can tap, type, open apps on, or screenshot it. Android supports full automation via Android's Accessibility Service; iOS is limited by Apple's own sandboxing to opening apps only - see the Mobile SDK's CONSTRAINTS.md for the full, honest breakdown of what each platform can and can't do.
helpPage.faqPara1: "No active providers yet" when creating an agent - you should not see this on a new account: every new account runs on the platform's hosted pool for its first 3 months, and the Free plan does after that. It appears once you are on a paid plan using your own provider - activate one under Connect → Providers.
helpPage.faqPara2: Ask AI button gives an error - same cause as above. It only fails when your account is off the hosted pool and has no active provider of its own.
helpPage.faqPara3: A pending WhatsApp/Telegram sender never gets a reply - check Admin → Channels for a pairing waiting on your approval.
helpPage.faqPara4: A tool doesn't show up for an agent - confirm it's enabled under MCP Tools, and that the agent's tool-access list either includes it or is left empty (unrestricted).
helpPage.gettingStartedPara1: You don't need an API key to start: a hosted model is already included, and Free-tier agents run on the platform's shared pool automatically. If your plan allows your own provider, go to Connect → Providers, pick Anthropic, OpenAI, or another supported provider, and paste in your own API key from that provider's dashboard. The key is validated with a real (non-billed) call before it's saved, and encrypted at rest - once it shows ACTIVE, your agents use it instead of the hosted pool.
helpPage.gettingStartedPara2: After that, the natural build order is: create an Agent (Build → Agents), try it privately in the Playground (Test → Playground), then either wire it into a Workflow for multi-step automation, or connect it directly to a channel (WhatsApp, Telegram, email) so real people can talk to it.
helpPage.introHint: A complete walkthrough of every part of the console. New here? The welcome tour (the "?" button in the top right of any page) covers the short version - this page has the full detail.
helpPage.knowledgePara1: Upload .md, PDF, Word, images (OCR), or audio/video (transcribed) files and they're chunked and embedded into a searchable vector store. Collections are folders you can nest and scope agents to - e.g. a "Returns Policy" collection only certain agents can search, versus a "Public FAQ" collection every agent can use.
helpPage.knowledgePara2: An agent only searches its knowledge base if "Attach knowledge base" is checked when creating it (or toggled on later from the Agents page), and only within whatever collections its knowledge-access allow-list permits.
helpPage.researchPara1: Where it is switched on, Research takes one question, runs several web searches, reads the most useful pages and writes a report. Each claim carries a marker such as [S1] that opens the source, and the Sources list shows the exact passage that was quoted. A run keeps going if you close the tab, and you can save the report as Markdown (PDF and Word on paid plans). Any agent can do the same in chat once Deep research is turned on in its Capabilities.
helpPage.researchPara2: Every run has limits, shown on the Research page before you start: a fixed number of web searches and page reads, a time limit for each research pass, and a number of runs per day. A report marked Partial hit one of those limits or could not read some pages. The citation check compares wording only - it confirms that a quote really appears in the source, not that the source itself is right, so read the sources for anything that matters.
helpPage.toolsPara1: A marketplace of Model Context Protocol servers and built-in tools an agent can call mid-conversation (web search, a database, the filesystem, your own custom scripts...). Enable the ones you want available, then scope which agents can actually use them from each agent's tool-access editor. Disabling a server here immediately removes it from every agent's available tools, even ones that previously had it checked.
helpPage.workflowsPara1: The visual canvas for multi-step automation: drag nodes (Trigger, Agent, Knowledge Search, Condition, Output, Device Control, and more) and connect them. Every node calls the real service behind it - a Workflow run genuinely calls your agent, genuinely searches your knowledge base, genuinely sends the WhatsApp message.
helpPage.workflowsPara2: Workflows can start three ways: manually (the "Run" button), on a schedule (cron expression, e.g. "every morning at 8am"), or via a webhook URL you can call from any external system. Every run is logged step-by-step under that workflow's Runs tab, including each individual tool call an Agent node made along the way.

helpPrimer.card_ask_body: Good agents know their limits: they pause for a human to approve high-stakes actions, so you stay in control of what actually happens.
helpPrimer.card_plan_body: An agent breaks a goal into steps, decides what to do next, and works across your channels — where a chatbot just replies to the last message.
helpPrimer.card_tools_body: Agents call APIs, search your documents, run code, and update systems — taking multiple steps to finish a job rather than only producing text.
helpPrimer.docsBody: The full reference — getting started, agents, workflows, knowledge, tools & MCP, channels, plans, security, and troubleshooting — with jump-links into every screen.
helpPrimer.intro: A chatbot answers a question and stops. An agent is different: it plans a path to a goal, uses tools to get real work done, takes multiple steps on its own, works across channels like chat, email, and voice, and asks a human when a decision truly matters. The shorthand: a chatbot talks, an agent does.
helpPrimer.learnBody: The fastest way to understand agents is to build one. On {brand} you can stand up a real, working agent for free in an afternoon, ground it in your own documents so it answers from what you know, and use code intelligence to learn directly from real codebases. From there you add the parts that make an agent trustworthy — guardrails that keep it in bounds and evaluation that measures whether it is actually doing the job well. It is hands-on the whole way: you learn agentic AI by shipping one.
helpPrimer.nowBody: The industry is shifting from AI that talks to AI that does. Instead of a clever autocomplete, you get a teammate that can carry a task from start to finish — drafting, checking, calling systems, and following up. Major analysts, including Gartner and Deloitte, expect enterprises to adopt AI agents rapidly through 2026. The practical upshot for you is simpler: agents multiply what one person can get done.
helpPrimer.recipesBody: Real, buildable automations for advertising, call centers, UPI payments, retail, healthcare and more — mapped to {brand}'s workflow nodes.
helpPrimer.title: Agentic AI, in plain terms
helpPrimer.tourBody: New here, or want a refresher? Nine illustrated steps walk you through every part of the console, in about two minutes.
helpPrimer.worthBody: Directing AI is becoming the next core literacy — the way spreadsheets, the web, and mobile each became baseline skills in their turn. The workforce is being reshaped by the people who learn to direct agents, not replaced by them. Students and professionals who actually build with agents gain a compounding edge: every workflow you hand off well makes the next one easier to hand off too.

httpNode.bodyHintForm: A JSON object of fields is encoded as key=value&… for you; anything else is sent exactly as typed.
httpNode.bodyHintJson: Sent with Content-Type: application/json unless you set your own Content-Type header.
httpNode.failOnHttpErrorLabel: Treat non-2xx responses as failures (the node is skipped and its input passes through)
httpNode.httpDescription: Call any public REST API or webhook - method, URL, headers, body - and pass the response on.
httpNode.insertSecret: Insert a vault secret as a header…
httpNode.saveAsHint: Blank: the response body becomes this node's output. A field name: the output is the input's own fields plus that field holding {status, ok, headers, body}, so later nodes can address both by name.
httpNode.secretsHintPrefix: Never paste a real key here. Store it in the vault and reference it as
httpNode.secretsHintSuffix: - the value is filled in server-side at run time and redacted from every response, log line and agent transcript.
httpNode.ssrfNote: Only public http(s) hosts are allowed: private, loopback and cloud-metadata addresses are refused, and redirects are followed for at most 3 hops. Responses are capped at 20,000 characters.
httpNode.templateHintInput: is this node's raw input; when it's a JSON object every top-level field is also addressable as
httpNode.templateHintJson: is the input as a JSON string literal, safe to embed inside a JSON body.

judgeCalibration.createHelp: Paste one comparison per line: input, answer A, answer B, which one a human preferred (A or B), and an optional reason. CSV or a copy from a spreadsheet both work. Quote any field that contains commas or line breaks. At least 20 rows are needed to run a set; 30 or more are recommended.
judgeCalibration.deleteBody: This removes the set, its rows and its calibration history. Eval runs are not affected. This cannot be undone.
judgeCalibration.description: Check that the LLM which grades your evals agrees with human reviewers. Kappa is agreement beyond chance (1 is perfect, 0 is no better than guessing); order-swap consistency shows whether the judge changes its mind when the two answers swap places.
judgeCalibration.historyHelp: Newest first. A falling kappa means the judge has drifted from your reviewers; re-run after changing the judge model.
judgeCalibration.kappaUndefined: Kappa is undefined for this set: the human labels or the judge used only one answer position throughout. Add rows where the preferred answer differs.

landing.earnPage_lede: There has never been a bigger gap between what businesses need and who can build it. Agentic AI closes that gap — and the people who learn it first get to be the ones businesses pay. This page is the honest playbook: what to learn, what it costs, how to deliver, and how to price.
landing.earnPage_mathNote: No invented success stories here — this is arithmetic, not a testimonial. The engagement dashboard and audit log give you the real numbers to show your client every month.
landing.earnPage_mathStep1: A shop misses ~20 orders a month outside opening hours. Average order ₹400 / $10 — that's real revenue walking away.
landing.earnPage_mathStep2: Your agent answers every channel 24/7 and captures even half of them: measurable new revenue every month, plus hours of answering repeated questions returned to the owner.
landing.earnPage_mathStep3: You charge a setup fee plus a monthly retainer that stays well below the value created — the owner profits from day one, and your revenue recurs. Ten clients like this is a real company.
landing.earnPage_mathSub: An illustrative example — your numbers will differ, and that's the point: you measure them.
landing.earnPage_partnerBody: We're building a formal partner program — commissions for builders who bring businesses onto VegaDūta, plus early access and co-marketing. It isn't live yet, and we won't pretend otherwise. Early builders get first access when it opens.
landing.earnPage_playbookSub: From zero to your first paying business customer.
landing.earnPage_s1Body: The Academy takes you from "what is an agent?" to shipping production workflows — 100+ lessons, hands-on labs, in plain language. No code needed to start; a real REST API, webhooks and MCP when you're ready to go deep. No card, no catch.
landing.earnPage_s2Body: One subscription gives you the factory: agents on WhatsApp, Email, Slack, Phone and Telegram, 100+ tool integrations, human-approval controls and a full audit log. Bring your own keys for frontier models — OpenAI, Gemini, Claude and more — so you control cost and capability, or start on the built-in model pool for free.
landing.earnPage_s3Body: Start local and specific: the shop that misses WhatsApp orders after 9pm, the clinic drowning in appointment calls, the coaching class that never follows up. Browse 248 ready-to-run workflow recipes across 89 industries to see what a first project looks like — then pick ONE business and ONE workflow.
landing.earnPage_s4Body: Describe the agent in a sentence and watch it build in Magic Studio, then harden it: ground it in the client's documents, set approval rules so nothing risky happens without a human, and hand the owner an audit log of every decision. Trust is the product — the automation is just how you deliver it.
landing.earnPage_s5Body: The old model bills time; the new model shares value. Measure what the agent actually does for the business — orders captured, hours saved, customers answered at 2am — put a number on it, and charge a fraction of that number every month. A setup fee plus an outcome-linked retainer is the pattern the best AI businesses use.

landing.faqA1FreeMode: Yes — free during our launch. Every feature is unlocked: agents, workflows and seats, WhatsApp, Telegram and Email, white-label branding. Pricing will be introduced later to sustain the infrastructure and the team, with advance notice; until then you are free to explore, experiment and run. Three ways to run models: bring your own keys, run on-device edge models at no cost, or use the platform pool on fair-use limits so your first agent answers without an API key.
landing.faq_a1: Yes — ₹0/$0, no card. Every feature is unlocked for 3 months for everyone who registers; after that you land on the Free plan, which is a real plan and not a countdown: 5 agents, 3 workflows, 2 seats, WhatsApp, Telegram and Email, and a hosted model included (30 messages/day) so your first agent answers without an API key.
landing.faq_a2: No. Every plan includes the platform's pooled hosted model, so your first agent works with zero setup. On paid plans you can bring your own key for any supported provider — including Sarvam for Indian languages — and your agents switch to it.
landing.faq_a3: Yes, on every plan including Free — you connect your own number via Meta's WhatsApp Cloud API or Twilio, and the agent answers there directly. We do not charge for the channel; the number and any Meta conversation fees stay yours. The conversations playing on this page are clearly-labelled simulations of that experience.
landing.faq_a4: All 22 scheduled Indian languages plus English and more — the console itself ships in 30 languages, and agents reply in the language the customer writes in. Voice in and out is available too, in the languages your chosen speech provider supports.
landing.faq_a5: You decide how much rope it gets. Set an agent's autonomy tier so consequential actions wait in your approval queue instead of just happening, guardrails and content moderation are built in, and every action lands in an audit log you can review any time.
landing.faq_a6: Two free paths: the live studio on this page builds something real from one sentence with no signup, and the VegaDūta Academy — 100+ free lessons with hands-on labs — takes you from zero to your first working agent.

landing.platform_p1_body: Nine native channel adapters feed one shared session, memory and approval pipeline — the same agent, with the same context, everywhere your customers already are.
landing.platform_p1_pt1: WhatsApp two ways — Meta Cloud API or Twilio — with outbound auto-routed to whichever connection is active.
landing.platform_p1_pt2: Voice calls and SMS on Twilio: live spoken replies over Twilio Conversation Relay, with per-caller memory that persists from call to call.
landing.platform_p1_pt3: Telegram, Slack, Discord, Instagram, Facebook Messenger, X (Twitter) DMs and email — native, webhook-verified adapters, not third-party glue.
landing.platform_p2_body: The entire official MCP registry — 18,000+ servers — is indexed into an instantly searchable catalog. Filesystem, fetch and browser-automation servers activate in one click; GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Postgres and Brave Search get an encrypted credential form.
landing.platform_p2_pt1: Each connected server runs as its own isolated process with a scrubbed environment — platform secrets are never handed to it.
landing.platform_p2_pt2: Defense in depth on every launch: launcher allowlist, blocked code-eval flags, SSRF-guarded URLs, per-tenant process caps.
landing.platform_p2_pt3: Connections are tenant-scoped, health-checked every five minutes, and reconnected automatically when a server drops.
landing.platform_p3_body: An experimental feedback-learning loop, off by default and opt-in per agent, can adjust model routing, prompt variants and tool subsets from feedback. Until you switch it on, your agent keeps its exact configured behavior.
landing.platform_p3_pt1: It is a preview feature that has not been proven in production, so treat it as an experiment, not a guarantee of better results.
landing.platform_p3_pt2: Every thumbs-up, rating or edit becomes training signal for the exact configuration that produced that answer.
landing.platform_p3_pt3: Your preference data exports as DPO pairs or KTO samples whenever you want to fine-tune offline. It stays yours.
landing.platform_p3_title: Experimental: agents that learn from feedback
landing.platform_row1_body: Every request runs through the same real pipeline — understand the brief, plan the steps, call the right tool, log the result. It's not a canned script, and it's the same execution path whether the channel is WhatsApp, email or a live phone call.
landing.platform_row1_title: The nervous system: brief → plan → action → outcome
landing.platform_row2_body: Every side-effecting step queues through a human-approval gate before it fires — with one honest exception: a live voice reply is spoken in the moment, not queued, because a phone call can't pause mid-sentence for a click.
landing.platform_row2_title: You approve the calls that matter
landing.platform_row3_body: Run inference on-device for free, bring your own model key, or use the platform's shared pool. Same agent, same behavior — just a different address for the thinking.
landing.platform_row5_body: An agent can hand off to one specialist colleague — one hop, by design. That colleague can't hand off again, so there's no runaway chain of agents delegating to each other.
landing.platform_row5_title: One hop to a specialist, by design
landing.platform_sub: How a brief becomes a real outcome — the pipeline, the approval gate, where it thinks, what it can reach, and how far it can delegate. Every line maps to shipped code, not a roadmap slide.

landing.pricing_free_sub: VegaDūta is an open-source agentic AI platform built by a small team. Every feature is unlocked for every account during launch — no tiers, no card. Explore, experiment and run. To sustain the infrastructure and the team we will introduce pricing later, with advance notice. Bring your own keys, run on-device edge models, or use the hosted pool — fair-use limits keep it fast for everyone.
landing.pricing_free_title: Open source. Free while we launch.
landing.pricing_plan1_f2: Hosted model included — no API key (30 msgs/day)
landing.pricing_plan1_tagline: Try the whole platform, no card required.
landing.pricing_plan2_f3: Bring your own key — any provider, incl. Sarvam
landing.pricing_plan3_f2: White-label branding, unlimited seats and agents
landing.pricing_plan3_f3: Unlimited knowledge collections, no edit lock
landing.pricing_sub: Every account that registers has everything unlocked for 3 months. After that the Free plan takes over — a real plan, not a trial, no card and no clock.
landing.pricing_subIN: ₹ pricing, UPI and cards via Razorpay. Every account that registers has everything unlocked for 3 months. After that the Free plan takes over — a real plan, not a trial, no card and no clock.
