landing.proof_lead: Every number below links to where you can count it yourself. Every persona is a starting point you customize — never a fixed template.
landing.proof_personasLabel: Define your own — these are starting points
landing.pw_closing: One platform, three places to think, and no lock-in in any direction. Start on the free hosted model, move to your own key when it pays for itself, and pull a model onto your own device the day that matters more than speed.
landing.pw_code_does1: Ask AI in Custom Code Tools drafts a tool on your device — one self-contained Java class or Python module, sandboxed with no file, network or process access.
landing.pw_code_does2: The platform re-checks that code before you keep it. The device is never trusted to certify its own output, and a check that fails to run counts as a failure, not a pass.
landing.pw_code_does3: An on-device model gets the same tools a cloud model gets. It proposes the call; the server executes it through the same approval gate, step ceiling and audit log.
landing.pw_code_does4: For real repository work, proposed file changes land in a scratch workspace and wait for a tenant admin to approve them — then you read the unified diff of exactly what landed.
landing.pw_code_does5: If a turn is too big for your device, it escalates to the cloud instead of failing.
landing.pw_code_footnote: Code-workspace tools stay off until you switch them on for a specific agent, and that agent needs an explicit repository grant — an empty grant denies everything.
landing.pw_code_never1: It never writes to your repository or your branch. The workspace is a throwaway clone and nothing is ever pushed back.
landing.pw_code_never2: It never opens a pull request. No part of this platform creates one.
landing.pw_code_never3: It never reads your codebase itself. Code search runs on the server against an index, and the device only sees the passages that come back.
landing.pw_code_never4: It never runs your builds or tests on its own. Those execute server-side, only after approval, and never hand their output straight back to the model.
landing.pw_code_never5: It is never the default. On-device needs an explicit opt-in and weights you have already chosen to download.
landing.pw_code_sub: This is the part people do not believe, so here is exactly how far it goes and exactly where it stops. Both columns describe the same feature.
landing.pw_code_title: Yes — a model on your own device can write tool code for you.
landing.pw_ctaLearn: See how the AI layer works
landing.pw_device_body: Switch on on-device mode and the weights are downloaded once into your browser, then answers are generated locally on WebGPU. Chrome's own built-in model can be used the same way. When a turn is too big for the device, it escalates to the cloud instead of failing.
landing.pw_device_title: A model that never leaves the machine you are sitting at.
landing.pw_device_weights: We do not host or train these models. WebLLM pulls the weights from the upstream MLC / Hugging Face CDN, and nothing downloads or runs on your device until you turn it on.
landing.pw_door1_body: The model runs in your browser on WebGPU, and the router never calls a server to produce the answer.
landing.pw_door2_body: {count} language-model providers you can connect with your own account and your own billing.
landing.pw_door3_body: The free plan's hosted model — 30 messages a day, no API key, nothing to configure.
landing.pw_eyebrow: Models, providers and where they run
landing.pw_g_llmNote: Every one of these is configurable today. None of them is a coming-soon card.
landing.pw_g_voiceNote: Listening and speaking are separate from the brain — choose them per agent.
landing.pw_note_attach: Adding a key does not switch these on everywhere. You attach voice or transcription to the specific agents that should have it, the same way you attach a knowledge base — and ElevenLabs needs at least one cloned voice before it can speak.
landing.pw_note_byok: Connecting your own key is a Premium capability. On the Free plan you do not need one at all — every agent routes through our shared hosted pool, 30 messages a day, with nothing to configure.
landing.pw_p_anthropic: Claude models on your own Anthropic key — the provider this platform is built and tested against.
landing.pw_p_azure: GPT models served from your own Azure OpenAI deployment and region.
landing.pw_p_bedrock: Models served through your Amazon Bedrock account and IAM credentials.
landing.pw_p_chromeAi: Chrome's built-in on-device model, used when the browser offers it.
landing.pw_p_deepseek: DeepSeek's own models, on a key from DeepSeek.
landing.pw_p_e2b: Short Python, Node or Bash snippets in a fresh disposable sandbox. Not a chat provider — this key unlocks the run_code tool.
landing.pw_p_elevenlabs: Agents speak replies aloud in a voice you have cloned in your own ElevenLabs account.
landing.pw_p_embeddings: Five local sentence-transformers models power your knowledge base. Embeddings run on CPU here, never through a paid hosted API.
landing.pw_p_gemini: Google's Gemini models on a direct AI Studio key. No GCP project needed.
landing.pw_p_groq: Open models served on Groq's fast-inference cloud. A different company from Grok.
landing.pw_p_meta: Muse Spark models directly from Meta, on a Meta Model API key.
landing.pw_p_mistral: Mistral's own models, on a key from Mistral AI.
landing.pw_p_ollama: Point an agent at open models you host yourself. Your server, your network, no cloud key.
landing.pw_p_openai: GPT models via your OpenAI account, also used for image generation.
landing.pw_p_openaiWhisper: Video-to-text using the OpenAI key you have already connected.
landing.pw_p_openrouter: One key, many labs. Routes to dozens of models through a single API.
landing.pw_p_sarvam: Chat models built for Indic languages — one key also covers translation, transliteration and language detection across 22 Indian languages.
landing.pw_p_sarvamVoice: Speech-to-text and text-to-speech on your Sarvam key. Spoken replies on live calls are currently Indian English; the speak tool can ask for another language.
landing.pw_p_vertex: Gemini and more through your own Google Cloud project — text, images and video.
landing.pw_p_webllm: Open models compiled for WebGPU, running inside the browser tab.
landing.pw_p_whisper: Self-hosted faster-whisper running on our own sidecar. Transcription with no key and no vendor.
landing.pw_sub: The brain is not welded in. Every agent you build can point at a provider you pay directly, at the model pool we host for free, or at a model that never leaves your laptop — and you can change your mind later without rebuilding the agent.
landing.pw_title: Bring your own key. Use ours. Or run it on your own machine.
landing.sdlc_bullet1Body: Code search runs on tree-sitter AST chunking, not fuzzy text matching — agents can trace callers, callees, and the full impact graph of a function before anyone touches it.
landing.sdlc_bullet1Lead: Ask it “what calls this?” and get a real answer.
landing.sdlc_bullet2Body: A dedicated workspace/execution loop lets an agent create an isolated git worktree, run your code, apply a fix, and diff the result — the same run → fail → apply → rerun cycle a human would use.
landing.sdlc_bullet2Lead: Agents can run code, not just suggest it.
landing.sdlc_bullet3Body: Executing code and applying changes each sit behind their own human-approval gate — the agent proposes, you approve, nothing lands unattended.
landing.sdlc_bullet3Lead: Every run and every apply is a checkpoint, not a rubber stamp.
landing.sdlc_bullet4Body: The same code intelligence is reachable over MCP, so it's not locked to VegaDūta's built-in agents — plug it into whatever agent tooling you already run.
landing.sdlc_card1_body: Semantic code search plus real caller/callee and blast-radius tools (search_code, code_callers, code_impact). Ask in Slack, get file:line citations — or an honest “not found”, never a plausible guess.
landing.sdlc_card1_title: “Where does this happen?” — answered from your code graph
landing.sdlc_card2_body: A supervisor reads per-file summaries and wakes only the specialists a PR needs — security, data/migrations, API contract. Each one checks real call sites before commenting. The agent comments; it never approves or merges.
landing.sdlc_card2_title: PR review routed to specialist reviewers
landing.sdlc_card3_body: The run_code tool executes short Python, Node or Bash snippets in a fresh E2B sandbox and reads back stdout/stderr — so an agent verifies logic actually works before telling you it does.
landing.sdlc_card3_title: Run code in a disposable sandbox
landing.sdlc_card4_body: code_callers separates “in the lockfile” from “actually reachable from our code”. The minimal bump is prepared and test-proven in an isolated workspace — and a human approves each repo's exact diff before anything lands.
landing.sdlc_card4_title: Dependency & CVE bumps, approved diff by diff
landing.sdlc_card5_body: The tag range — not memory — sets the scope. Breaking changes are verified against actual callers via code_impact, grouped by audience, and held at an approval gate: the agent drafts, a human publishes.
landing.sdlc_card5_title: Release notes from the real commit range
landing.sdlc_card6_body: Nightly failures are triaged one by one — flake, environment or real break — with the root cause traced to a suspect file. Flake fixes are drafted in a sandbox and re-run N times to prove stability before any human reviews the PR.
landing.sdlc_footerNote: GitHub and GitLab are reached the honest way — through MCP servers from the registry (open PRs, review diffs, file issues), not a bolt-on you have to trust blindly. Eight ready-to-adapt recipes show the full builds: agents, tools, guardrails and cost tiers.
landing.sdlc_sub: Not keyword search dressed up as intelligence — your agents query a real AST-parsed map of your repo, trace the blast radius of a change, and execute inside an isolated workspace that never moves without your sign-off.
landing.sdlc_title: Agents that actually know your codebase
landing.security_auth_body: Sign-in runs on Keycloak (OAuth2 / OIDC with PKCE). We never see or store your password.
landing.security_data_body: Full data export and erasure on request — you stay in control of your information.
landing.security_rest_body: Provider keys & channel secrets are AES-encrypted in the database — never stored in plain text.
landing.security_sub: Your conversations and your data are protected at every layer of VegaDūta's agentic AI platform.
landing.security_tenant_body: Every workspace's data lives in its own isolated schema — no cross-tenant leakage.
landing.security_transport_body: Served entirely over HTTPS through Cloudflare's global edge network.
landing.security_verified_body: Email verification is required before any dashboard access.
landing.sh_app_body: Describe an app and App Studio builds a multi-page phone app you can preview live, with camera, Bluetooth, vibration and sharing. Plug in your own agents and workflows without writing a backend, then publish it with its own sign-in for your customers.
landing.sh_app_title: Say the app. Hold it in your hand.
landing.sh_ctaSignup: Open all six — create free account
landing.sh_enterprise_body: Single sign-on through your own identity provider and SCIM user provisioning for each workspace, plus abuse shielding (captcha challenges, IP and user blocklists) in front of the whole platform.
landing.sh_foot: Status comes from the deploy log, not a brochure. Not claimed here, because it is not true yet: outbound calling, an embeddable web-chat widget, and agents collecting UPI payments into your own account.
landing.sh_powered_body: A “Powered by” chip in the playground, quick tasks and Build names the exact model behind each answer. No black box and no silent swaps.
landing.sh_powered_title: You always see which model answered.
landing.sh_sales_body: A built-in leads CRM, bulk email sent straight from a workflow, reply and bounce detection, and agents that run on a schedule with a full run history. Capture the lead, follow up, and see who answered, all in one place.
landing.sh_sales_title: A sales desk that never sleeps.
landing.sh_sales_where: Workflows → CRM lead · Bulk email · Schedules
landing.sh_sub: No roadmap slides. Everything below is live on vegaduta.ai today: shipped, not promised.
landing.sh_team_body: Mid-conversation, an agent can hand the chat to a specialist agent (billing, tech support, sales) along a bounded chain, and every handoff is written to the audit trail. Agents also speak the open A2A protocol with signed agent cards.
landing.sh_team_title: Agents that know when to ask a colleague.
landing.sh_title: Six new jobs it learned this month.
landing.sh_versions_body: Every change to an agent is kept as a version. Tag the one you trust as Production, and restore any earlier version in a click if a new prompt behaves worse than the old one.
landing.smb_boutique_note: First to reply is usually first to sell.
landing.smb_boutique_problem: New stock drops, DMs flood in, and by the time you reply the size is already sold out.
landing.smb_boutique_solution: The agent shares stock and price instantly, books a fitting slot, and follows up on abandoned carts.
landing.smb_dental_note: No-shows drop when the reminder does the nagging.
landing.smb_dental_problem: Front desk is on a call, three more are on hold, and a slot just went unbooked.
landing.smb_dental_solution: The agent answers on WhatsApp or phone, books the free slot, and sends a reminder the day before.
landing.smb_kirana_note: Answer every message in seconds, day or night.
landing.smb_kirana_problem: Orders pile up on WhatsApp after 9pm — you reply next morning, customer's gone.
landing.smb_kirana_solution: Your agent replies instantly in Hindi, takes the order, sends a UPI link, and confirms the delivery slot.
landing.smb_restaurant_note: Never miss an order because the line was busy.
landing.smb_restaurant_problem: Peak dinner rush — phone's ringing, WhatsApp's pinging, and orders get missed either way.
landing.smb_restaurant_solution: Your agent takes the order, confirms the table, and collects payment by UPI — hands stay in the kitchen.
landing.smb_sub: Pick your business. See the fix in seconds.
landing.smb_title: Built for how small businesses run
landing.smb_titleIN: Built for how India does business
landing.smb_tuition_note: Say it once. The agent repeats it a thousand times.
landing.smb_tuition_problem: Parents ask the same fee/timing questions on ten different chats — every single day.
landing.smb_tuition_solution: One agent answers every parent at once, in their language, and nudges fee due-dates automatically.
landing.solo_card1_body: Configure an agent for a specific job — support, content, ops — instead of learning a sprawling suite of features you'll only ever touch a corner of.
landing.solo_card1_title: Pick a role, not a platform.
landing.solo_card2_body: Consequential actions — sending a message, spending, deploying a change — route through an approval step you control, so “automated” never means “unsupervised”.
landing.solo_card2_title: Automation with a checkpoint, not a blind spot.
landing.solo_card3_body: Connect existing tools through the MCP registry, or describe a custom tool in plain language and let the platform generate the code for it.
landing.solo_card3_title: No engineering team to stand it up.
landing.solo_card4_body: No pricing built around a headcount you don't have — see current tiers below.
landing.solo_sub: You don't need to hire to get coverage — pick an agent for the job, connect the tools you already use, and keep a hand on the wheel for anything that actually matters.
landing.solo_title: Run it like you've got a team
landing.sovereignty_byokBody: Bring your own Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini or other provider credential — you're billed directly by that provider, not marked up.
landing.sovereignty_byokCta: Start free, bring your key later
landing.sovereignty_checkChecking: Checking whether this browser can run a model locally…
landing.sovereignty_checkNo: This browser can't run a model locally yet — Chrome or Edge on a laptop or desktop can. The shared pool works everywhere in the meantime.
landing.sovereignty_checkOk: This browser can run VegaDūta Edge — WebGPU detected. Replies can run right here, free, with nothing sent to a server for the answer.
landing.sovereignty_closingBody: The same approval gates and tool permissions apply no matter where the thinking happens.
landing.sovereignty_deviceBody: Inference runs locally in the browser, free, with nothing sent to a server for the reply itself.
landing.sovereignty_hostedBody: No key to manage — the platform's own hosted pool handles it, metered against your plan.
landing.sovereignty_hostedCta: Start free on the shared pool
landing.sovereignty_limitBody: On-device is a preference, not a guarantee — a turn that needs more than your device can handle falls through to the shared pool automatically, so a reply is never just left hanging.
landing.sovereignty_savedNote: Your choice is remembered on this device and applied the first time you chat.
landing.sovereignty_sub: Run the same agent on your own device for free, with your own model key, or on the platform's shared pool — the behavior doesn't change, only the address of the thinking does.
landing.sparkBadgeFreeMode: Agentic AI · BYOK or free edge models · hosted pool for experiments
landing.stats_disclaimer: No invented numbers on this page — every stat links to where you can count it
landing.sx_ctaSignup: Open all six — create free account
landing.sx_evals_body: Score an agent against your own test set with six automated judges, with confidence intervals so one lucky run doesn't fool you. Set a pass bar, and a version that falls short is not promoted.
landing.sx_evals_title: A new version has to earn Production.
landing.sx_flow_body: Pin a step's output while you build, so the steps after it run on the same data. Expressions pass values between steps, draft runs stay separate from production, and long jobs run in the background while you do something else.
landing.sx_foot: Status comes from the deploy log, not a brochure. Not claimed here, because it is not true yet: outbound calling, agents collecting UPI payments into your own account, and store listings for the mobile apps.
landing.sx_lab_body: Agent Lab draws any past run as a graph of every model call and tool call. Re-run it from the step you choose, remove parts of the prompt to see which ones the answer depends on, and repeat an input to check that it answers the same way twice.
landing.sx_lab_title: See exactly why it said that.
landing.sx_memory_body: One page lists what your agents have learned about you. Edit what is wrong, delete what you don't want kept, and write the notes you want every conversation to start with.
landing.sx_skills_body: Fourteen built-in skills, from customer support and SQL to Word, Excel and PDF files, each a plain SKILL.md folder. An agent reads the full instructions only when a task calls for them. It can also draft new skills from its own successful runs, and those stay off until an admin approves them.
landing.sx_skills_title: Skills it picks up only when it needs them.
landing.sx_sub: Building an agent takes a sentence. Knowing it will behave takes evidence. Everything below is live in VegaDūta today.
landing.sx_teams_body: Give an agent two or more specialist colleagues and it splits a job between them at the same time, then combines the answers. Delegation goes one level deep, each branch has a time limit, and the whole team shares one run budget.
landing.sx_teams_title: One lead, a team behind it.
landing.sx_title: Six ways it got easier to trust this month.
landing.templates_banner: Submissions are sanitised (no keys, no private data) and human-reviewed before they appear — no unvetted prompts in the gallery.
landing.templates_mech1_blurb: Any approved agent or workflow template becomes a private, editable copy in your workspace — inspect everything before you run it, then make it yours.
landing.templates_mech2_blurb: Built something your shop or team runs on? Submit it from your console — the platform strips your keys and private data, and a reviewer checks it before it goes public.
landing.templates_sub: A public gallery of agent and workflow templates shared by VegaDūta members — browsable by anyone, importable in one click, and reviewed before anything is published.
landing.templates_title: Don't start from a blank page
landing.uc_all: Browse the full catalogue — 89 industries of workflow recipes
landing.uc_code_brief: Review every pull request against the call graph, post the findings, and hold the merge for my approval.
landing.uc_invoice_brief: Chase each unpaid invoice on WhatsApp with a UPI link — disputes come to me, receipts go out on their own.
landing.uc_oncall_brief: When an alert webhook fires, dedupe it, write the incident summary and page the on-call — after my confirm.
landing.uc_research_brief: Take one research question, fan it into sub-questions, search in parallel and return a brief with sources.
landing.uc_sub: Every card is a real brief you can run verbatim — “Run this spec” drops the sentence into the live studio on this page, no signup. The recipe link opens the full step-by-step in the workflow-recipes guide.
landing.uc_support_brief: Answer customer questions on WhatsApp and email from our own docs, and hand off to a human when unsure.
landing.uc_title: Six jobs that are one sentence away.
landing.uc_voice_brief: Answer every call, book the slot on the calendar and text the confirmation. Spoken-language coverage depends on the speech provider you connect.
landing.underneath_agents_body: An agent is four things: a system prompt, tools, channels, and an autonomy tier you control — it takes orders and books slots, it doesn't just chat. A workflow is trigger → nodes → action on a real engine (Temporal), and every request runs the same real pipeline whether the channel is WhatsApp, email, or a live call.
landing.underneath_agents_title: Agents that actually run your business
landing.underneath_channels_body: WhatsApp three ways, voice calls and SMS, Telegram, Slack, Discord, Instagram, Messenger, X and email — native adapters sharing one memory, so every channel is the same agent. Your customers already have WhatsApp; there's no separate integration to build and host before they can talk to it.
landing.underneath_codeintel_body: Full-repo search, call-graph tracing, and blast-radius checks before any edit — then the change runs in an isolated workspace and queues through the same human-approval gate as every other side-effecting action.
landing.underneath_codeintel_title: Understands your codebase, not just your prompt
landing.underneath_guardrails_body: Every side-effecting step queues through a human-approval gate before it fires — a live voice reply is the one exception, since a call can't pause mid-sentence. Policy-pack content moderation ships with a human review queue, not something you bolt on after an incident.
landing.underneath_guardrails_title: Guardrails and approval, included from day one
landing.underneath_learning_body: Flip on shared memory per agent and what one agent learns becomes available to the rest of your team, isolated per tenant. Self-tuning from feedback is experimental and off by default, so your agent keeps its configured behavior until you opt in.
landing.underneath_learning_title: Gets smarter, when you opt in
landing.underneath_mcp_body: The entire official MCP registry is indexed into a searchable catalog — filesystem and browser-automation servers activate in one click, GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Postgres and Brave Search get an encrypted credential form. Your own agents can be exposed as MCP tools other systems call, too.
landing.underneath_media_body: Prompt-to-image on Gemini and Vertex AI, and short Veo video clips — generated inside any agent or the live studio, with industry-tailored prompts to start from.
landing.underneath_media_title: Images and video, in the same box
landing.underneath_models_body: Run inference on-device for free, bring your own key across 14 providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Bedrock, Vertex AI, Mistral, Groq, Ollama and more — or use the platform's shared pool. Same agent, same behavior, just a different address for the thinking.
landing.underneath_models_title: Start free, then bring any model
landing.underneath_ops_body: Metrics and logs on managed cloud monitoring, audit trails on every action, and a console that degrades gracefully instead of erroring. An agent can hand off to exactly one specialist colleague — one hop, by design — so there's no runaway chain of agents delegating to each other.
landing.underneath_ops_title: Boring, in the good way — with one hop of help
landing.upi_sub: One UPI payment quietly triggers a whole chain of work: order confirmation, a WhatsApp receipt, your sales ledger, and a ping to you — no one lifts a finger.
landing.upi_title: When a customer pays, your agent does the rest — automatically.

landing.whySwitch_p1_contrast: Generic workflow builders give you nodes and connectors — you still have to build and host your own channel integration before a single customer can actually talk to it.
landing.whySwitch_p2_contrast: A no-code AI app builder gets you a hosted app or a chat window. Here, the same sentence creates a real agent with tools, a workflow behind it, and a live number your customers can message today.
landing.whySwitch_p2_us: One prompt becomes an agent, a workflow, AND a deployed channel
landing.whySwitch_p3_contrast: Most builders leave moderation, approval gates and retries as something you assemble yourself out of extra nodes. This platform runs on a Temporal-backed engine with policy-pack guardrails from day one.
landing.whySwitch_p3_us: Guardrails and a real workflow engine, included
landing.whySwitch_sub: Tools like n8n and no-code AI app builders are great at what they're built for. VegaDūta is built for a different job: give a real business a real agent, live on the channels its customers already use.
landing.whySwitch_title: Not another node-based builder, or a one-off AI app generator
landing.wn_c1: Approvals — risky actions park for your yes
landing.wn_c2: Guardrails — PII, jailbreak and policy checks on every turn
landing.wn_c3: Budgets — spend caps that stop, not warn
landing.wn_c4: Models — your keys, on-device edge, or the hosted pool
landing.wn_c5: Channels — WhatsApp, Telegram, email, voice and more
landing.wn_c6: Audit — every action traced and replayable
landing.wn_c8: Source — the code is going public; read, fork, self-host
landing.wn_diyBody: Then you know the catch: you are the platform. Hosting, model keys, guardrails, approvals, budgets — and wiring real channels — is a DIY project. VegaDūta is the same idea productised, with the platform parts built in.
landing.wn_keep1: Instant answers about anything, zero setup
landing.wn_keep3: A free tier you already have
landing.wn_keepFoot: Assistants help you inside their window. They won't answer your customer on WhatsApp, wait three days for your approval, or keep a workflow running while you sleep.
landing.wn_keepTitle: What your chat app does better — honestly
landing.wn_linkCompare: Compare with n8n, Dify and Botpress →
landing.wn_sub: ChatGPT, Claude Desktop, Hermes, OpenClaw — all good tools. The difference isn't intelligence, it's jurisdiction: an assistant helps you inside its window; an agentic platform works for you, on your customers' channels, under your rules.
landing.workforce_devBody: Ship agents, not scripts: MCP-native tools, a real REST API, webhooks, and every prompt, tool call and decision logged. The Academy takes you from your first agent to production patterns — free and hands-on.
landing.workforce_devTitle: Make agentic AI the first line on your CV
landing.workforce_everyoneLine: Coding or not, everyone can learn this: 100+ free Academy lessons take you from zero to your first working agent — no card, no catch.
landing.workforce_everyoneNoCode: No code — brief it in a sentence
landing.workforce_execBody: Gartner expects 40% of enterprise apps to carry task-specific AI agents by end of 2026 — up from under 5% in 2025. Pilot one on a real workflow this week: no procurement cycle, human approval on every consequential step, free to start.
landing.workforce_execTitle: Your competitors are already hiring a robot workforce
landing.workforce_lead: The layoffs are real — and so is the boom on the other side. In 2025, US employers cut more jobs citing AI than ever before, while pay for people with AI skills pulled away from everyone else's. The difference isn't luck — it's whether you can put agents to work.
landing.workforce_newsBody: Salesforce cut its support team from 9,000 to 5,000 as AI agents took over about half of customer interactions — CEO Marc Benioff: “I need less heads.”

Calls shown as VegaDūta (included) run on the platform-hosted pool that your plan's usage allowance covers.

index.embedderOff: On-device AI is switched off for this deployment, so local code search can't run here.
index.enableEmbedderHint: Downloads the embedding model that turns your files into a searchable index. It happens once on this device, only when you press this, and the model never leaves it.

index.installedNow: Local search is ready on this device.
index.needEmbedder: Searching your code needs a small embedding model on this device, and it isn't here yet. Nothing downloads until you press the button below.
index.restored: An index of {files} files ({chunks} chunks) from an earlier visit is still on this device — you can ask questions now, or open the folder again to refresh it.

model.edgeOffBody: Answering runs only on your machine, and on-device AI is switched off for this deployment — so there is no model this page could ask, and no hosted one it is willing to fall back to. Opening and indexing a folder still work; asking does not.
model.edgeOffTitle: On-device AI is off in this build
model.notReadyBody: Answers here run entirely on your machine, so a model has to be installed first. This page never starts a download on its own — choose and download one in the Edge console, then come back.
model.notReadyTitle: No on-device model is ready yet

privacy.body: The folder you open is read by this browser tab alone. File contents, the search index and your questions are never sent to VegaDūta or anywhere else, and the reply is generated by the model installed on this machine.
privacy.free: Free — nothing here spends your hosted quota, because nothing here is ever sent to a server to be answered.
privacy.signIn: The console around this page needs a VegaDūta sign-in, but the page itself never reads your account, your plan or your tenant.
privacy.title: Everything here stays on your device

repo.body: Choose the project you want to ask about. Your browser asks for permission first, and you can withdraw it at any time.

repo.stayHere: Files stay on this device — nothing is uploaded.

localModelSettings.batchHelp: How many prompt tokens the model chews at once — larger is faster on capable hardware.
localModelSettings.contextHelp: How much of the conversation the model can see at once. A bigger window keeps long chats and tool results intact and uses more memory.
localModelSettings.contextLoaded: Loaded with {loaded} tokens; the Assistant asks for {wanted}.
localModelSettings.contextNotLoaded: The model is not loaded right now; the Assistant asks for {wanted} tokens.
localModelSettings.contextShort: Ollama loaded fewer tokens than the Assistant asks for ({wanted}), so long conversations and tool results get cut off. Choose a context window above: it is made for you in a few seconds, without downloading anything.
localModelSettings.keepHelp: A model that is not loaded takes several seconds to start on the next message. Longer keeps your answers fast and uses memory while it waits.
localModelSettings.parallelHelp: How many requests the model can serve at once — raise it if turns wait behind each other.
localModelSettings.reasoningHelp: Models like Qwen 3.5 reason silently before they reply. Off answers in seconds; higher settings think longer and can answer harder questions better, but a laptop may take 30 seconds or more.
localModelSettings.saveFailed: Could not save the setting. Try again.
localModelSettings.saved: Saved. It applies from your next message.
localModelSettings.timeoutHelp: How long a turn may run before it is cut off.
localModelSettings.title: Speed and behaviour
localModelSettings.toolDeferralHelp: Hide most tool schemas until the model searches for them — a much smaller prompt, one extra step when a tool is needed.

nodeConfigDrawer.adaptiveRoutingOnHint: This agent's runs in this workflow let the reinforcement-learning policy pick the model per turn. Manage exploration rate/algorithm from the agent's Learning tab.
nodeConfigDrawer.adaptiveRoutingUpdateError: Could not update adaptive model routing.
nodeConfigDrawer.adminOnlyEnforcedHint: Enforced by the server, not just this screen - anyone else who tries to approve or reject this request (including via the API directly) will be rejected.
nodeConfigDrawer.adminOnlyLabel: Only a tenant admin may approve this
nodeConfigDrawer.approvalMessageHint: Shown alongside the request in the Approvals inbox - optional, leave blank for none.
nodeConfigDrawer.approvalMessagePlaceholder: e.g. Double-check the refund amount against the original order before approving.

nodeConfigDrawer.bulkEmailSourceItems: A list from the previous step
nodeConfigDrawer.bulkEmailThrottleHint: A run sends for at most about 90 seconds; recipients that would exceed the rate are reported as deferred rather than sent faster.

nodeConfigDrawer.emailHint: Requires an SMTP relay configured for this deployment (see the README).

nodeConfigDrawer.noToolsHint: No tools available - check this agent's allowed-tools list and enabled MCP servers.

nodeConfigDrawer.payloadLabel: Payload (optional - blank uses this node's input)
nodeConfigDrawer.pdfHint: Generated as a real PDF (via the output-generator module) from this run's text output - not just a renamed text file.

nodeConfigDrawer.pollError: Could not update the poll trigger.

nodeConfigDrawer.voiceMenuHint: Runs on a live phone call: speaks the prompt, waits for keypad digits, then follows the branch matching what the caller pressed. Only works on a workflow whose Trigger is bound to the Phone call channel.
nodeConfigDrawer.voiceMenuInvalidPromptPlaceholder: e.g. Sorry, that wasn't a valid option. Press 1 for sales, 2 for support.
nodeConfigDrawer.voiceMenuNumDigitsHint: Set to 1 for a single-key menu. Leave blank to collect a longer entry (e.g. an account number) that ends when the caller presses the finish key.
nodeConfigDrawer.voiceMenuPromptPlaceholder: e.g. Press 1 for sales, 2 for support.
nodeConfigDrawer.webhookUpdateError: Could not update this trigger node's webhook.
nodeConfigDrawer.whatsappHint: Sends from this tenant's own Twilio WhatsApp number - set that up on the Channels page first.
nodeConfigDrawer.workflowTriggerHint: Runs the selected workflow synchronously with this node's input, then continues using that run's last step as this node's output. If the triggered run fails or pauses for approval, this node is marked skipped (with the reason in its log) - the parent run keeps going rather than halting automatically. Triggering a chain back on itself is blocked (this workflow is excluded from the list above, and an indirect cycle through other workflows is refused at run time), with a hard 5-level depth cap either way.

nodeConfigExtra.pollTriggerSummary: Or poll an HTTP endpoint on an interval

nodeDefs.agentDescription: Runs a configured agent against the current input.
nodeDefs.approvalDescription: Pauses the run for a human sign-off via the Approvals inbox.
nodeDefs.bulk_emailDescription: Sends a personalized email to many recipients - throttled, with an unsubscribe link, a suppression list and reply detection.
nodeDefs.codeDescription: Applies a built-in transform (extract a field, regex replace, template, case, JSON parse/stringify) - not arbitrary code.
nodeDefs.conditionDescription: Branches true/false on whether input contains a phrase.
nodeDefs.crm_leadDescription: Creates or updates a lead in the Leads CRM, moves it to a pipeline stage, or adds an activity to its timeline.
nodeDefs.data_tableDescription: Reads or writes rows in a data table - the workspace's built-in spreadsheet store - so a workflow can keep state between runs.
nodeDefs.device_controlDescription: Queues a command (tap, type, open app) for a paired phone - fire-and-forget, see the run log.
nodeDefs.fan_outDescription: Runs the very next node once per item in a list, all at the same time - like Loop, but concurrent - merging the results into an array.
nodeDefs.human_inputDescription: Pauses the run to collect structured data (a form) from a person, then resumes with the answers.
nodeDefs.knowledgeDescription: Retrieves context from a knowledge collection.
nodeDefs.loopDescription: Repeats the very next node once per item in a list, collecting every result into an array.
nodeDefs.outputDescription: Sends the result out - log it, or publish a workflow event.
nodeDefs.parallelDescription: Runs every connected branch at the same time against the same input, then merges the results.
nodeDefs.sub_flowDescription: Runs a whole embedded sub-graph once per item in a list - multi-step iteration, merging results into an array.
nodeDefs.supervisorDescription: An agent picks one of several named routes based on the input - like Condition, but the decision is made by the model.
nodeDefs.toolDescription: Calls one specific tool from a chosen agent's toolkit directly - no LLM turn needed.
nodeDefs.triggerDescription: Starts a run - inbound message, schedule, or manual.
nodeDefs.voice_menuDescription: A phone-call menu: speaks a prompt, collects keypad (DTMF) digits with a timeout and retries, then branches on what the caller pressed.
nodeDefs.workflowDescription: Runs a different, already-saved workflow synchronously and uses its result as this node's output.

onboardingTour.stepBuildBody: Agents are the AI personalities that answer chats - give one a system prompt (or click "Ask AI" next to that field to have it drafted for you) and a provider. Knowledge Base holds the .md/PDF/docs an agent can search before answering. Workflows chain agents, tools, and channels together on a visual canvas - most automations belong here, not in a single agent.
onboardingTour.stepConnectBody: Providers is where you activate an LLM (Anthropic, OpenAI, etc.) with your own API key - do this first, nothing else works without it. MCP Tools is a marketplace of extra capabilities (web search, databases, file access...) you can turn on for agents to use. Devices pairs a phone to let workflows control it directly.
onboardingTour.stepReadyBody: Every page also has a "?" Help button in the top-right that reopens this briefing or takes you to the full written guide with more detail on every screen.
onboardingTour.stepTestBody: Playground is a private chat window to try an agent before it's live. Once you're happy, connect it to WhatsApp, Telegram, or email from the Admin > Channels page so real customers can reach it.
onboardingTour.stepWelcomeBody: This console has four jobs, in the order you'll actually use them: get oriented, build, connect, and test. The floating orb in the corner is your nav - hover it any time to see every station.

continuationPasses.description: How many more times the model is asked to carry on when its reply stopped at a step it announced but did not take.
continuationPasses.help: Raise it for agents that often announce a step and stop. Each extra pass costs a model call.
continuationPasses.label: Extra passes after an unfinished reply

maxToolSteps.description: The most tool calls one turn may make before it is stopped and asked to answer with what it has.
maxToolSteps.help: Raise it for agents that do long multi-step jobs. Lower it to stop runaway loops and keep cost predictable. The value shown for a workspace or the platform is the base figure for a standard agent: an agent's autonomy tier scales it at run time, so a more or less autonomous agent may use a different number. An agent's own value is used exactly as set.
maxToolSteps.label: Most tool calls per turn

retrievalMinScore.description: How relevant a knowledge passage must be to be returned. 0 returns every hit.
retrievalMinScore.help: Raise it if the agent quotes irrelevant passages. Too high and it may find nothing.
retrievalMinScore.label: Least relevance for a passage

retrievalTopK.description: How many passages one knowledge-base search returns to the agent.
retrievalTopK.help: More passages give the agent more to work with but cost more tokens and can add noise. Fewer are faster and cheaper.
retrievalTopK.label: Knowledge passages per search

toolOutputMaxChars.description: How many characters of one tool result are passed to the model; the rest is cut.
toolOutputMaxChars.help: Raise it when the agent needs to read long documents or API responses in full, at the price of more tokens per turn. Lower it to save cost.
toolOutputMaxChars.label: Longest tool result

toolTimeoutSeconds.description: How long a single tool call may run before it is stopped. The platform default has no limit; each tool then keeps its own timeout.
toolTimeoutSeconds.help: Set a limit if one slow tool can hold up whole conversations. Whether a stopped call had any effect is unknown, so the agent is told not to assume it worked.
toolTimeoutSeconds.label: Longest time per tool call

turnTimeoutSeconds.description: How long one turn may run before it is stopped.
turnTimeoutSeconds.help: Raise it for slow research or code tasks. A turn that runs out of time ends with what was done so far.
turnTimeoutSeconds.label: Longest time per turn

autonomousMultiplier.description: A fully autonomous agent gets the turn's tool-call limit multiplied by this number.
autonomousMultiplier.help: Raise it for agents that run long jobs without a person watching; they can then spend more calls and money in one turn. 1 gives them the standard limit.
autonomousMultiplier.label: Fully autonomous agents get N times the limit

graceCalls.description: How many more tool calls the model may attempt after the turn's tool limit is used up. Each one is refused with a note to answer with what it has; past this number the turn is stopped with an error.
graceCalls.help: Raise it if a model needs a few tries to stop calling tools. Lower it to end looping turns sooner. 0 stops the turn at the first call over the limit.
graceCalls.label: Calls answered after the limit

supervisedDivisor.description: A supervised agent gets the turn's tool-call limit divided by this number, but never less than the minimum below.
supervisedDivisor.help: Raise it to keep supervised agents on a shorter leash. 1 gives them the full limit.
supervisedDivisor.label: Supervised agents get 1/N of the tool limit

supervisedMinSteps.description: The smallest tool-call limit a supervised agent gets, however high the number above is.
supervisedMinSteps.help: Keep it at 3 or more so a supervised agent can still finish a simple job with several steps.
supervisedMinSteps.label: Least tool calls for a supervised agent

enabled.description: When a person approves an action, the agent finishes the task by itself instead of waiting for a new message.
enabled.help: Turn it off if you want every approved action to end the turn and be followed up manually.
enabled.label: Carry on after an approval

jobsContinueAfterDenial.description: When a person denies an action in a background job, the job carries on with the denial noted instead of stopping.
jobsContinueAfterDenial.help: Leave it off if a denial should stop the job. Turn it on when the job can usually finish without the denied step.
jobsContinueAfterDenial.label: Background jobs continue after a denial

ttl.description: How long an approval request waits for a decision before it expires. 0 means requests never expire.
ttl.help: With no expiry, forgotten requests stay open indefinitely and the agent keeps waiting. An expired request counts as not approved.
ttl.label: Approval requests expire after

useAgentModel.description: Summaries, assists and context compaction use the same model as the agent they work for, when no model is chosen for them.
useAgentModel.help: Turn it off to let the platform choose a model for these calls, which may be cheaper or a different provider.
useAgentModel.label: Background calls use the agent's model

maxAudioMb.description: The biggest audio file a person can attach to a chat message, in megabytes. The platform also has an overall file limit that this cannot exceed.
maxAudioMb.help: Raise it for longer recordings; large files are slower to send and use more of the model's allowance.
maxAudioMb.label: Largest audio upload (MB)

maxDocumentMb.description: The biggest document or spreadsheet a person can attach to a chat message, in megabytes. The platform also has an overall file limit that this cannot exceed.
maxDocumentMb.help: Raise it for long reports and large data files; large files are slower to process.
maxDocumentMb.label: Largest document upload (MB)

maxImageMb.description: The biggest image a person can attach to a chat message, in megabytes. The platform also has an overall file limit that this cannot exceed.
maxImageMb.help: Raise it for photos and screenshots; large files are slower to send and use more of the model's allowance.
maxImageMb.label: Largest image upload (MB)

maxVideoMb.description: The biggest video a person can attach to a chat message, in megabytes. The platform also has an overall file limit that this cannot exceed.
maxVideoMb.help: Raise it for longer clips; large files are slower to send and use more of the model's allowance.
maxVideoMb.label: Largest video upload (MB)

contextTurns.description: How many earlier turns are compared when deciding whether a message is a repeat that can reuse a stored reply.
contextTurns.help: More turns make a match stricter and cache hits rarer.
contextTurns.label: Earlier turns that identify a repeat

eligibleWithTools.description: Allow stored replies to be reused for agents that have tools. Off by default because a tool may return something different next time.
eligibleWithTools.help: Turn it on only when the tools are read-only and slow-changing, and you want faster, cheaper repeat answers. People may see an answer that is not current.
eligibleWithTools.label: Reuse replies for agents with tools

heuristicEnabled.description: Ask the model to carry on when a reply sounds as if it stopped before doing what it said it would.
heuristicEnabled.help: Turn it off if the nudges trigger on replies that were meant to end.
heuristicEnabled.label: Nudge on unfinished wording

enabled.description: When a reply is cut off by the model's length limit or ends in a broken tool call, ask the model to carry on or retry.
enabled.help: Turn it off only to diagnose a model problem; people then see cut-off replies as they are.
enabled.label: Finish cut-off replies

maxContinuations.description: How many times the model is asked to carry on after its reply was cut off.
maxContinuations.help: Each continuation is another model call. Raise it for long answers, lower it to save cost.
maxContinuations.label: Most continuations of a cut-off reply

maxToolCallRetries.description: How many times the model is asked to repeat a tool call that arrived with unusable arguments.
maxToolCallRetries.help: A retry costs a model call. 0 gives up at the first broken call.
maxToolCallRetries.label: Most retries of a broken tool call

keepPrimaryModel.description: A short follow-up in a conversation that already used tools stays on the agent's main model instead of the cheaper one.
keepPrimaryModel.help: Turn it off to let cost routing send follow-ups such as 'yes' to the cheaper model, at the risk of weaker handling of a task in progress.
keepPrimaryModel.label: Keep the main model for follow-ups

maxStickyTools.description: The most tools carried over into a short follow-up message. 0 keeps none.
maxStickyTools.help: A higher number helps when a task uses many tools, a lower one keeps the tool list small.
maxStickyTools.label: Most tools kept on offer in follow-ups

stickyToolsEnabled.description: Keep offering the tools the conversation already used when the next message is a short follow-up.
stickyToolsEnabled.help: Turn it off if short replies such as 'yes' should start from the normal tool selection.
stickyToolsEnabled.label: Keep tools on offer in follow-ups

stickyToolsWindow.description: How long after use a tool stays on offer for short follow-up messages.
stickyToolsWindow.help: A longer window helps long working sessions, a shorter one keeps the tool list small.
stickyToolsWindow.label: How long follow-up tools stay on offer

maxAttempts.description: How many times a model call is tried when the provider fails or is busy, including the first try.
maxAttempts.help: More attempts hide short provider outages but make a failing request slower to report an error.
maxAttempts.label: Attempts per model call

maxEntriesPerAgent.description: How many answers one agent keeps for reuse. The oldest are dropped beyond this.
maxEntriesPerAgent.help: A larger store finds more repeats and uses more storage.
maxEntriesPerAgent.label: Most stored answers per agent

similarityThreshold.description: For agents that reuse answers to similar questions: how close a new question must be to an earlier one, from 0.85 to 1, for the stored answer to be served.
similarityThreshold.help: A lower number serves more repeats but risks giving an answer meant for a different question. Keep it high when wrong answers are costly. An answer is only reused for the person it was given to.
similarityThreshold.label: How alike a question must be to reuse an answer

ttl.description: How long a stored answer can be served to a similar question before it is dropped.
ttl.help: Shorten it when your answers go out of date quickly.
ttl.label: How long a reusable answer is kept

enabled.description: Store a short record of each turn's tool calls with the conversation, so later turns can see what was done.
enabled.help: Turn it off to keep conversation history text-only; the agent then cannot tell what its tools did in earlier turns. This applies to the whole workspace.
enabled.label: Keep a record of tool calls in the conversation

maxEntriesPerTurn.description: How many of one turn's tool calls are written into the record. Further calls are only counted.
maxEntriesPerTurn.help: Raise it for turns that make many calls and need every one remembered.
maxEntriesPerTurn.label: Tool calls listed per turn

maxReplayCharsPerTurn.description: How many characters of one turn's record are shown to the model; the rest is counted, not listed.
maxReplayCharsPerTurn.help: Lower it to save cost on every later turn, raise it to keep more detail.
maxReplayCharsPerTurn.label: Longest tool record per turn

replayEnabled.description: Include the stored record of earlier tool calls when the model is given the conversation.
replayEnabled.help: Turn it off to keep storing the record without using any of the model's working space for it.
replayEnabled.label: Show the tool record to the model

replayTurns.description: How many of the most recent turns that used tools have their record shown to the model.
replayTurns.help: A larger number helps in long working sessions but uses more of the model's working space.
replayTurns.label: Earlier turns whose tool record is shown

maxPromptTokensPerTurn.description: Total prompt tokens one reply's tool loop may send the model before it is told to stop calling tools and answer with what it has.
maxPromptTokensPerTurn.help: 0 means no cap. Lower it to stop a runaway tool loop that keeps resending a large context; the per-turn tool-call limit bounds rounds, this bounds their size.
maxPromptTokensPerTurn.label: Prompt-token budget per reply

enabled.description: In a long tool run, replace older tool results with a short placeholder so the conversation stays within the model's limit.
enabled.help: Turn it off if the agent must see every earlier result; long runs may then hit the model's size limit.
enabled.label: Clear old tool results

thresholdChars.description: How large the tool results in a turn may grow before older ones are cleared.
thresholdChars.help: Raise it to keep more results visible, lower it to keep long runs small and cheap.
thresholdChars.label: Size that triggers clearing

branchTimeoutSeconds.description: How long one delegated sub-task may run before it is reported as timed out.
branchTimeoutSeconds.help: Raise it for slow sub-tasks. A hung sub-task never holds up the whole answer past this time.
branchTimeoutSeconds.label: Longest time per sub-task

maxBranches.description: How many sub-tasks or helper agents one delegation call may start at once. Extra ones are reported as over the limit.
maxBranches.help: Raise it for broad research jobs, lower it to keep cost and load down.
maxBranches.label: Most parallel sub-tasks

agent-limits.description: How much work one agent turn may do before it is stopped.
agent-limits.label: Agent limits

approvals.description: What happens after a person approves or denies an action, and how long a request waits.
approvals.label: Approvals

attachments.description: How large the files people attach to chat messages may be.
attachments.label: Chat uploads

aux.description: Which model summaries, assists and compaction use.
aux.label: Background model calls

chat.description: How a reply is finished, retried, cached and continued.
chat.label: Conversation behaviour

delegation.description: How much work an agent may hand to other agents at once.
delegation.label: Delegation

guardrails.description: How strict the automatic safety checks are. These can only be made stricter than the platform setting.
guardrails.label: Safety checks

knowledge.description: How widely a search of your uploaded documents gathers candidates before it picks the best passages.
knowledge.label: Knowledge search

learning.description: How the agent's learning policies try out different options.
learning.label: Learning

memory.description: How many memories an agent keeps and recalls.
memory.label: Memory

providers.description: How connected AI provider keys are used when one stops working.
providers.label: AI providers

quality.description: How test runs and the AI judge behave.
quality.label: Evaluation

routing.description: Which messages count as simple enough for the faster model.
routing.label: Model routing

skills.description: How much of the agent's instructions the list of installed skills may use.
skills.label: Skills

tools.description: Which built-in tool helpers an agent keeps.
tools.label: Agent tools

failMode.description: What happens when a safety check itself fails, for example the judge model is down. Closed refuses the action; open lets it through.
failMode.help: You can only make this stricter than the platform setting. Closed protects against someone making a check fail on purpose, at the price of refusing work during an outage.
failMode.label: When a safety check breaks

maxScannedChars.description: How much of a message or reply is scanned for jailbreak patterns. Text beyond it is not scanned.
maxScannedChars.help: You can only raise this above the platform value. A wider window stops attacks hidden behind padding at the cost of a little more processing.
maxScannedChars.label: Text scanned for jailbreak attempts

maxInputChars.description: How much of the checked text the AI safety judges read. Text beyond it is not judged.
maxInputChars.help: You can only raise this above the platform value. Raising it judges long tool results in full but makes each judge call larger.
maxInputChars.label: Text shown to the safety judge

readOnlyCalls.description: Whether an agent on the Supervised autonomy tier still asks you before a tool that only reads, such as a search or a lookup. Writes, sends and tools the platform has not classified always ask.
readOnlyCalls.help: You can only make this stricter than the platform setting. Asking every time is the safest choice; letting read-only tools run removes a prompt but also a chance to stop a search you did not expect. An agent that can read private data, take in untrusted content and send data out is asked about every call whatever this says.
readOnlyCalls.label: Supervised agents and read-only tools

options.auto-allow: Let read-only tools run without asking

failMode.description: What the check that reviews risky tool calls does when it cannot give a verdict. Inherit follows the setting for safety checks above.
failMode.help: You can only make this stricter than the platform setting. Closed refuses the tool call if the check fails.
failMode.label: When the tool-call check breaks

options.open: Open: let the tool call through

blockScore.description: Content scoring at or above this on the judge's 0 to 100 toxicity scale is blocked. A lower number blocks more.
blockScore.help: You can only lower this, never raise it above the platform value. A very low value blocks ordinary frank wording.
blockScore.label: Toxicity score that blocks

candidatePoolMax.description: The ceiling on how many candidate passages one knowledge search gathers, however many results are requested.
candidatePoolMax.help: This protects speed and cost when an agent asks for many results at once. Raise it only if answers miss relevant passages in large knowledge bases.
candidatePoolMax.label: Most candidates per search

candidatePoolMultiplier.description: How many candidate passages a knowledge search gathers for every passage it finally returns.
candidatePoolMultiplier.help: A higher number gives the ranking more to choose from, which helps when many documents are similar, but every search takes more time and compute. Lower it if searches feel slow. This does not change how many passages the agent sees.
candidatePoolMultiplier.label: Search breadth per result

maxMemories.description: How many memories one agent may keep. The oldest and least used are dropped beyond this.
maxMemories.help: Raise it for assistants that should remember a lot about people; this also raises storage and recall cost.
maxMemories.label: Most memories per agent

maxFacts.description: How many memories are handed to an on-device session when it starts.
maxFacts.help: On-device models have a small working space, so keep this low.
maxFacts.label: Memories given to on-device chat

recallMaxFacts.description: The most facts an agent is shown from its relationship memory in one lookup.
recallMaxFacts.help: More facts give the agent more background about a person or topic but use more of its working space. Fewer keep answers focused. Set it for the whole workspace, or for one agent that needs more or less.
recallMaxFacts.label: Facts recalled from graph memory

recallMaxPaths.description: How many connections in the memory graph are read to find the facts for one lookup.
recallMaxPaths.help: Several connections can lead to the same fact, so densely linked memories may need a higher number to find everything. A higher number makes each lookup slower.
recallMaxPaths.label: Graph paths read per lookup

agentTopK.description: How many of the agent's own memories are looked up for each message.
agentTopK.help: More memories give more context but use more tokens.
agentTopK.label: Agent memories recalled per turn

tenantTopK.description: How many memories shared across the workspace are looked up for each message.
tenantTopK.help: More memories give more context but use more tokens.
tenantTopK.label: Shared memories recalled per turn

maxMemories.description: How many memories shared across the workspace are kept. The oldest are dropped beyond this.
maxMemories.help: Raise it for large teams that rely on shared knowledge; it also raises storage and recall cost. This applies to the whole workspace.
maxMemories.label: Most shared memories

rejectedCooldown.description: How long background work skips a connected provider key after the provider refused it.
rejectedCooldown.help: While paused, scheduled and automatic jobs use another connected provider, or wait, instead of calling a key that keeps failing. People chatting are never blocked and always see the provider's real error. When the pause ends, one call is let through to check whether the key was fixed. Zero turns the pause off.
rejectedCooldown.label: Pause after a provider refuses a key

defaultMode.description: Whether an evaluation run replays the agent with its tools in a safe sandbox (full pipeline), or answers in text only (quick), when the run or its dataset does not say.
defaultMode.help: The full pipeline tests what your users get, including tool use, and costs more. In it, tools that only read really run; anything that could change data, send a message or spend money is simulated and listed in the run. Quick is cheaper and says nothing about tool use.
defaultMode.label: How evaluations run

defaultRepeats.description: How many times each test case is run when a run does not say. More repeats show how consistent the agent is.
defaultRepeats.help: Every repeat multiplies the cost and time of a run.
defaultRepeats.label: Repeats per test case

callTimeoutSeconds.description: How long one judge call may take before it counts as failed.
callTimeoutSeconds.help: Raise it if a slower model often times out; failed calls make evaluation results incomplete.
callTimeoutSeconds.label: Longest time per judge call

model.description: The model used to judge evaluation runs. Leave blank to let the platform choose from what your workspace already uses.
model.help: Use a stronger model for more reliable grades or a cheaper one to save cost. The model must be available on your connected provider.
model.label: Model for the AI judge

defaultExplorationRate.description: The share of turns a newly created learning policy spends trying a random option.
defaultExplorationRate.help: This only sets the starting point for policies created from now on. Existing policies keep their own rate, which you change per agent where the policy is managed. Zero means a new policy never explores at the start.
defaultExplorationRate.label: Starting exploration rate for new policies

ucb1ExplorationConstant.description: How strongly a learning policy that uses the confidence-bound method favours options it has tried less often.
ucb1ExplorationConstant.help: Zero always picks the option with the best average so far. Higher values keep trying other options for longer before settling. The default is the textbook balance. Only policies that use this method are affected.
ucb1ExplorationConstant.label: Willingness to try less-tested options

maxChars.description: A message longer than this is never treated as simple. Simple messages can go to a faster, cheaper model.
maxChars.help: Lower it to send more messages to the main model for quality; raise it to save cost.
maxChars.label: Longest simple message

maxClauses.description: A message with more sentences than this is never treated as simple.
maxClauses.help: Lower it to send more messages to the main model for quality.
maxClauses.label: Most sentences in a simple message

maxBlockChars.description: How many characters the list of skills may take in the agent's instructions. When it is full, later skills are shortened to their names.
maxBlockChars.help: Raise it to keep descriptions for more skills, lower it to save tokens on every turn. This applies to the whole workspace.
maxBlockChars.label: Size of the skills list in the prompt

maxSkills.description: How many of your skills are named in the agent's instructions so it knows they exist. The rest are counted, not listed.
maxSkills.help: Raise it if you have many skills; each listed skill uses a little of the model's working space on every turn. This applies to the whole workspace.
maxSkills.label: Most skills listed in the prompt

enabled.description: Give the agent its scratchpad tools: a persistent notepad with session-scoped working notes and a long-term pad it writes and reads itself.
enabled.help: Turn it off to remove the four scratchpad tools (write, read, list, delete) from the agent. Notes already stored are kept but the agent can no longer reach them.
enabled.label: Agent scratchpad

skillsPage.customEmptyMember: No custom skills yet. A workspace admin can add them.
skillsPage.deleteConfirmBody: Agents will stop using this skill immediately. This can't be undone, so export it first if you may want it back.
skillsPage.editHint: A skill's name can't be changed after it is created. To add or change bundled files, upload the skill again as a .zip.
skillsPage.genericError: That didn't work. Please try again.
skillsPage.howItWorks: A skill is a set of instructions for one kind of task. Agents see only each skill's name and description; when a request matches, the agent loads the full instructions, and reads any bundled files only if it needs them. So you can add many skills without slowing agents down or raising cost on unrelated chats.
skillsPage.importedNotice: Imported "{name}". Agents will use it from their next message.
skillsPage.importedWithSkipped: Imported "{name}". {count} file(s) were skipped because they are not text.
skillsPage.improvementHint: Applying replaces this skill's instructions for every agent. Discarding leaves the live skill untouched.
skillsPage.newHint: The name uses lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens (64 characters max). The description decides when agents use this skill, so say what it does and when to use it (1,024 characters max).
skillsPage.pageSubtitle: Packaged expertise your agents load only when a task needs it.
skillsPage.replaceConfirmBody: This workspace already has a skill with that name. Replacing it overwrites its instructions and bundled files.
skillsPage.reviewAckHighRisk: I read the findings and want to approve this high-risk skill anyway.
skillsPage.reviewAdminOnly: Only a workspace admin can approve or reject a skill.
skillsPage.reviewBannerBody: This skill's content no longer matches what {by} approved on {date}. Review what changed before agents rely on it.
skillsPage.reviewBannerBodyAuto: This skill's content no longer matches the version that was accepted automatically on {date}, when it was first {how}. Review what changed before agents rely on it.
skillsPage.reviewBannerNoRecord: This skill's content no longer matches the version that was approved. Review what changed before agents rely on it.
skillsPage.reviewBannerUnapprovedBody: A security scan rated this skill high risk and nobody has approved it yet. Read the findings below before agents rely on it.
skillsPage.reviewBannerUnapprovedTitle: Flagged high risk and not approved
skillsPage.reviewConflict: This skill changed again while you were reviewing it. The latest version is shown - review it before approving.
skillsPage.reviewEnforcedNote: Paused: agents can't load this skill until it is approved.
skillsPage.reviewOffNote: This skill is switched off, so agents cannot use it and it is not in the review queue. Switch it on to review it again.
skillsPage.reviewQueueSummary: {count} skill(s) need your review (changed since approval, or flagged high risk and not approved): {names}.
skillsPage.reviewRejectedNotice: Turned off "{name}". Agents will not use it.
skillsPage.reviewWarnOnlyNote: Agents can still use this skill. Your workspace only warns for now, so nothing is blocked until enforcement is turned on.
skillsPage.riskBadgeTitle: Static scan result: {level}. A scan reduces risk; it does not prove a skill is safe.
skillsPage.ruleCovertAction: Asks the agent to act without telling the user
skillsPage.ruleCredentialRequest: Asks for passwords, keys or tokens
skillsPage.ruleDescriptionDirective: Description tries to steer when the skill is used
skillsPage.ruleDisableSafeguards: Asks the agent to bypass approvals, guardrails or logging
skillsPage.ruleDisguisedFileName: File name with a disguised extension
skillsPage.ruleEmbeddedIpUrl: Web address that uses a raw IP address
skillsPage.ruleEncodedText: Readable text hidden in an encoded block
skillsPage.ruleExfiltrateData: Asks the agent to send private data out
skillsPage.ruleHiddenUnicodeTag: Invisible text hidden in the skill (Unicode tag characters)
skillsPage.ruleMarkdownImageExfil: Image link that can carry data out
skillsPage.ruleMetadataMismatch: Description does not match what the instructions do
skillsPage.ruleObfuscatedText: Wording hidden behind invisible or look-alike characters
skillsPage.ruleOutboundTransfer: Asks the agent to send something to an outside address
skillsPage.ruleOverrideInstructions: Tells the agent to ignore or override its instructions
skillsPage.rulePathTraversalName: File name that escapes the skill folder
skillsPage.ruleRemoteScriptPipe: Downloads a script and runs it
skillsPage.ruleRevealSystemPrompt: Asks the agent to reveal its system prompt
skillsPage.ruleRoleHijack: Tries to change the agent's role or rules
skillsPage.ruleScanTruncated: Part of the skill was too large to scan
skillsPage.ruleSensitiveFileName: File name that looks like a secret
skillsPage.ruleSensitivePath: Touches credential files or secret stores
skillsPage.ruleSuspiciousEndpoint: Web address of a known data-collection or webhook service
skillsPage.ruleUrlUserinfo: Web address with embedded login details
skillsPage.savedNotice: Saved "{name}". Agents will use it from their next message.
skillsPage.scanBuiltInNote: Built-in skills ship with the platform and are reviewed by us. They are scanned here for information only and are never paused.
skillsPage.scanDialogIntro: Nothing has been saved yet. Review what the scan found, then confirm or cancel.
skillsPage.scanDialogReplaces: Confirming replaces your existing skill with the same name.
skillsPage.scanDisclaimer: A scan reduces risk; it does not prove a skill is safe. It looks for hidden characters, instructions that try to override an agent, requests to send data out and similar patterns. Read what a skill tells your agents to do before you rely on it.
skillsPage.scanNoFindings: No flags raised. That is not a guarantee, so skim the instructions yourself.
skillsPage.scanTruncated: Only the most serious findings are shown.
skillsPage.securityModeEnforcing: Skill security: enforcement is on. A changed or unapproved high-risk skill is paused until an admin approves it.
skillsPage.securityModeWarnOnly: Skill security: warn-only. Skills are scanned and changes are flagged, but nothing is paused.
skillsPage.selectPrompt: Select a skill to read its instructions.

studioPage.clipBodyMotion: Motion+: an agent imagines a short keyframe sequence, and your device fills in the motion between them — agent-directed animation, free and rendered entirely on your device. Prefer something simpler? Still turns any photo into a pan-and-zoom clip in one click. Neither is cinematic AI footage — both are honest, stylised motion.
studioPage.clipBodyStill: Turn a still image into a short pan-and-zoom motion clip, rendered entirely in your browser — nothing is uploaded and there is no per-clip charge. A stylised motion clip, not cinematic AI footage.
studioPage.galleryEmptyBody: Ask any agent to generate an image in the Playground — it shows up here the moment it's ready.
studioPage.idea1: a steaming cup of masala chai on a rainy windowsill
studioPage.idea2: a friendly robot shopkeeper in a bustling bazaar
studioPage.idea3: a minimalist mountain at sunrise for a travel brand

studioPage.imageBody: Any of your agents can create images — just ask in chat, e.g. "generate an image of a sunrise over Bengaluru". It lands in your gallery above, on your Files page, and ready to animate in Clip Studio.
studioPage.pageSubtitle: A running gallery of what your AI staff have already created — plus two free, on-device ways to turn it into motion.

templateSetupGuide.adminOnly: Connecting servers, channels and credentials is restricted to workspace admins. If that is not you, send this list to whoever administers the workspace.
templateSetupGuide.cautionSmartHome: This one moves things in your actual home. Read exactly what your Home Assistant exposes before switching it on, and keep the agent supervised.
templateSetupGuide.checkFailed: We could not read this workspace's setup, so nothing below is ticked off. The steps themselves are still accurate.
templateSetupGuide.checking: Checking what this workspace already has…
templateSetupGuide.footerHint: Nothing is created until you name the agent and submit the form.
templateSetupGuide.mcpDeployment: Needs {vars}, and only works if the deployment was set up for this server. Ask whoever runs it before promising anyone this will work.
templateSetupGuide.mcpEitherOr: Either one of these — you do not need both.
templateSetupGuide.mcpFindHint: On the Tools page, look for the card named “{name}”.
templateSetupGuide.mcpNeedsCredential: You will need: {vars}. Get this from the third-party account first — we cannot issue it.
templateSetupGuide.mcpNoCredential: No credentials to find. One click to switch it on.
templateSetupGuide.mcpOAuth: Sign-in happens on Atlassian's own consent screen. There is no key to paste, and a pasted token will not work.
templateSetupGuide.mcpSecretNote: Store keys in the workspace vault and reference them as {{secret.NAME}} from the server's config, so they resolve inside the tool boundary. Never paste a key into a chat with the agent.
templateSetupGuide.mcpServerPath: Needs {vars}, which is a file path on the server itself, not a value you can paste from your laptop. Whoever runs the deployment has to set this up.
templateSetupGuide.mcpStateError: On, but the last connection failed
templateSetupGuide.reasonBrowseSite: Opens a page the way a browser would, for sites with no API.
templateSetupGuide.reasonDatabase: Read-only queries against a database you point it at.
templateSetupGuide.reasonErrors: Pulls the actual stack traces and error groups rather than reasoning about a pasted fragment.
templateSetupGuide.reasonEscalate: For handing a conversation to a human — escalation only, not day-to-day answering.
templateSetupGuide.reasonRepo: Reads the repository this agent is supposed to reason about, instead of whatever it can infer from the conversation.
templateSetupGuide.reasonSmartHome: Controls the devices in your own Home Assistant setup.
templateSetupGuide.reasonTeamChat: Reads from and posts to your team's Slack.
templateSetupGuide.reasonWebSearch: Lets the agent look things up beyond what it was trained on.
templateSetupGuide.stepAllowListBody: MCP tools reach an agent under a prefixed name. This template does not set a tool allow-list, so anything you switch on above reaches it automatically — no extra step today.
templateSetupGuide.stepAllowListNamesNote: The moment you do restrict this agent's tools, the prefixed MCP names have to be in that list too, or they are silently dropped. The agent's own tool-access screen lists the real names.
templateSetupGuide.stepAllowListTitle: If you restrict this agent's tools later, include the MCP names
templateSetupGuide.stepChannelBody: This agent is meant to answer real customers, patients or staff, not just you in the console. Connect at least one inbound channel.
templateSetupGuide.stepChannelByoNote: WhatsApp, Telegram and Email are all available on the Free plan, but every channel is bring-your-own account — you supply the Meta, Twilio, Telegram or mailbox credentials.
templateSetupGuide.stepChannelTitle: Connect the channel your people actually write to
templateSetupGuide.stepCodeIntelBody: Without an index, the code-search tools return nothing and the agent quietly falls back to guessing — the one thing this template promises not to do.
templateSetupGuide.stepCodeIntelUncheckableNote: There is no endpoint that tells this page whether a repository is indexed, so this step is never ticked automatically. Check it yourself on the Code Intel page.
templateSetupGuide.stepCreateBody: Using this template pre-fills the create form on the Agents page. Review the instructions, change what does not match your business, name it and submit.
templateSetupGuide.stepCreateTitle: Create the agent and brief it
templateSetupGuide.stepE2bBody: Running code needs a workspace-level E2B credential and a configured code-execution template.
templateSetupGuide.stepE2bBothNote: Both halves are required, and so is the agent's own code-execution toggle. A key on its own leaves the tool listed but dead.
templateSetupGuide.stepE2bTitle: Add an E2B key and turn on code execution for this agent
templateSetupGuide.stepGoogleBody: One consent flow unlocks the built-in Gmail, Calendar, Drive and Sheets tools. Without it those tools are present but fail on first use.
templateSetupGuide.stepGoogleNotMcpNote: This is the supported Google path. It is not the same thing as the google-drive MCP server in the tools catalog, which needs a credentials file on the server host instead.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeBodyRecommended: This agent is noticeably better when it can quote your own material. Create a knowledge collection and upload what it should answer from.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeBodyRequired: This agent's whole job is answering from your material. Until a knowledge collection holds real content, it is no better than a plain chat model.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeContentNote: An empty collection does not count. The documents have to be uploaded and indexed before the agent can use them.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeFreeNote: The Free plan includes one knowledge collection.
templateSetupGuide.stepKnowledgeTitle: Upload the documents this agent should answer from
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpBody: A template cannot enable a server for you — there is no per-template or per-agent MCP setting in this product. Enable these on the Tools page and they reach every agent in the workspace.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpBodyNone: None. This agent works with what is already built in, and deliberately so — nothing here should be reaching a browser, a database or the open web.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpCapReached: You are at your plan's connector limit. Turn one off, or upgrade, before adding another — otherwise the request is simply refused.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpCatalogOnlyNote: Only servers from the built-in catalog are suggested. Anything else you add yourself needs a platform review before it can connect.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpExceedsFree: This template needs more connectors than the Free plan allows. It cannot be fully set up without upgrading.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpFreeCapNote: The Free plan allows two MCP connectors in total, and only ones from the built-in catalog.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpTitle: Switch on the MCP servers this agent needs
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpUsage: Connectors registered in this workspace: {used} of {cap}.
templateSetupGuide.stepMcpUsageUncapped: Connectors registered in this workspace: {used}. Your plan has no cap.
templateSetupGuide.subtitle: Picking a template fills in the agent's instructions and nothing else. Here is everything else that has to be in place before it does real work, in the order to do it.
