toolApproval.argsTruncated: These arguments are too long to show in full here, so this call cannot be approved from the chat. Review the full request in the approvals queue.
toolApproval.bulkHint: Decides the waiting calls one after another, oldest first, and stops at the first problem.
toolApproval.bulkStoppedError: Stopped after a problem; the calls below it are still waiting.
toolApproval.bulkStoppedTruncated: Stopped: the next call's arguments are too long to show here, so it waits for your own decision.
toolApproval.continueNotStarted: The agent was not restarted automatically after this decision. Send a message to have it carry on.
toolApproval.continueTimedOut: The agent has not finished carrying on yet. Its reply will be in the conversation when it does; reload to check.
toolApproval.continuing: The agent is carrying on with the task.
toolApproval.continuingLongWait: This is taking longer than usual, but the agent has not stopped. Its reply will appear here when it is done.
toolApproval.continuingRunning: The agent is working on the next step. Its reply appears here as soon as it is ready.
toolApproval.continuingStill: Still working. A model running on this computer can take a few minutes; you can keep reading meanwhile.
toolApproval.continuingWaiting: Your decision is recorded. The agent is picking the task back up.
toolApproval.decideError: Could not record your decision. Try again.
toolApproval.needsAdmin: A workspace admin must approve this.
toolApproval.noArguments: No arguments were recorded for this call.
toolApproval.notRunYet: The agent wants to run this action. It has not run yet.
toolApproval.queueMore: {count} more waiting. The next one appears when you decide this one.
toolApproval.rejected: Rejected. The action was not run.
toolApproval.title: Waiting for approval: {tool}

toolLabels.does_coding_task: Starts a coding task that can read and change files in a code workspace.
toolLabels.does_create_workflow: Creates a new workflow in this workspace.
toolLabels.does_data_table_query: Reads rows from one of this workspace's data tables.
toolLabels.does_data_table_write: Adds or changes rows in one of this workspace's data tables.
toolLabels.does_deep_research: Runs several web searches and reads the pages it finds.
toolLabels.does_delegate_parallel: Hands parts of the task to several agents and reads their answers.
toolLabels.does_delegate_to_specialist: Hands part of the task to another agent and reads its answer.
toolLabels.does_fetch_web_page: Downloads one public web page and reads its text.
toolLabels.does_http_request: Sends a request to a web address or API; depending on the request it can read or change something there.
toolLabels.does_http_request_write: Sends data to a web address, which can change something on that service.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_activate: Brings the named application to the foreground on this computer.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_click: Clicks a point or element on your screen.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_clipboard: Reads from or writes to the clipboard on this computer.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_elements: Lists the buttons and fields currently on screen (read-only).
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_key: Presses a key or a key combination (for example Cmd+S) on this computer.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_notify: Shows a notification on this computer.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_open: Opens an application, a file, or a web link on this computer.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_press: Presses a named button or menu on your screen.
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_screen: Captures what is currently on your screen (read-only).
toolLabels.does_local_desktop_type: Types text into the app currently in the foreground.
toolLabels.does_run_desktop_recipe: Replays a recorded run of desktop actions on this computer.
toolLabels.does_schedule_task: Sets up a task to run later or on a repeating schedule.
toolLabels.does_verify_citations: Compares quoted text with the web pages it was taken from.

toolPolicies.denyUnlisted: any argument not listed is refused
toolPolicies.editorHelp: One entry per tool, or per name pattern such as mcp__files__*. Each rule names an argument path (url, opts.limit, items[*].id) and checks: type, enum, minLength, maxLength, min, max, pattern, urlHostIn, pathUnder, maxItems, required, forbidden.
toolPolicies.errorEmpty: Enter a policy document, or use Remove all.
toolPolicies.errorPolicyShape: Policy {n} needs a tool name and a list of rules.
toolPolicies.errorShape: The document must be an object with a policies list.
toolPolicies.errorTooLarge: The document is larger than {max} characters.
toolPolicies.errorTooManyPolicies: At most {max} tools can have a policy.
toolPolicies.intro: Limit what this agent may pass to a tool. A call that breaks a rule is refused before the tool runs, and the agent is told why. Rules can only tighten what the agent may do, never grant more.
toolPolicies.none: No argument policies on this agent.
toolPolicies.refusalNote: A refused call appears in this agent's activity as the tool's result and in the audit log as tool.arg_policy.denied. Argument values are never written to the log.
toolPolicies.title: Tool argument policies

toolSecretGrants.adminOnlyNote: Only a workspace admin can change which secrets a tool may use.
toolSecretGrants.howToUseHint: In Python read secrets['NAME']; in Java call vega.Secrets.get('NAME'). The value is handed to the program when it runs and is never shown to the AI model.
toolSecretGrants.noneAvailable: No secrets are available to code tools. On the Secrets page, edit a workspace secret and turn on "Let code tools use this secret" - it is off by default, and personal secrets can never be used by a shared tool.
toolSecretGrants.saveFailedError: Could not update which secrets this tool may use.
toolSecretGrants.summaryNone: No secrets - this tool cannot sign in to anything

trajectoryEval.errorArgKey: Line {line}: argument names are field names joined by dots, like opts.limit.
trajectoryEval.errorArgsJson: Line {line}: the argument matchers are not valid JSON.
trajectoryEval.errorArgsObject: Line {line}: the argument matchers must be a JSON object.
trajectoryEval.errorMaxExtra: Max extra calls must be a whole number from 0 to 1000.
trajectoryEval.errorMinEfficiency: Min efficiency must be a number from 0 to 1.
trajectoryEval.errorMinScore: Pass at score must be a number from 0 to 1.
trajectoryEval.errorTooManyArgs: Line {line}: too many argument matchers on one step.
trajectoryEval.errorToolName: Line {line}: start with a tool name (letters, digits and _ - . : only).
trajectoryEval.intro: The tool calls this agent should make for this case, in order. One step per line: a tool name, optionally followed by a JSON object of argument matchers.
trajectoryEval.loadFailed: Could not load the expected trajectory.
trajectoryEval.modeExact: Exact: same calls, same order, nothing extra
trajectoryEval.modeInOrder: In order: extra calls allowed in between
trajectoryEval.noActual: The agent made no tool calls.
trajectoryEval.otherGrader: This case already has a response grader (regex, exact or JSON schema). A case holds one grader, so clear that one before adding an expected trajectory.
trajectoryEval.saveFailed: Could not save the expected trajectory.
trajectoryEval.saved: Expected trajectory saved. Run the dataset again to score it.
trajectoryEval.stepsHelp: An argument matcher is a literal value, {"regex":"..."}, {"present":true} or {"absent":true}. Leave the list empty to expect no tool calls.
trajectoryEval.toollessHint: This dataset replays without tools, so the trajectory is saved but cannot be scored. Turn on tool execution for the dataset to score it.
trajectoryEval.truncated: Only the first {max} actual calls are compared.
trajectoryEval.useActual: Use the actual calls as expected
trajectoryEval.useActualConfirm: Replace this case's expected trajectory with the tool names this run called?
trajectoryEval.usedActual: Expected trajectory replaced from this run. Edit it to add argument matchers, then run the dataset again.

troubleshoot.catalogMeta: {gb} GB download · wants ~{ram} GB RAM · tool calls: {grade}
troubleshoot.catalogSub: Open-weight models you can download for this install. This machine has {ram} GB RAM - pull a smaller one for a light machine, a bigger one for better answers.
troubleshoot.check.down: Whole app down or containers missing
troubleshoot.downBody: This page can only see what the browser reaches. If the app itself does not load, open a terminal in the install folder and run:
troubleshoot.modelMissing: {tag} is not downloaded yet - pull it below, then chat works.
troubleshoot.modelOk: {tag} is installed - agents can use it.
troubleshoot.probeFail: The probe failed - check that the model is fully downloaded.
troubleshoot.probeOk: Tool calls work ({grade}) - the model answered in {ms} ms.
troubleshoot.probeWarn: The model answered but did not make a structured tool call - agent features will be limited; pick a model marked 'structured' in the catalog.
troubleshoot.probing: Asking the model to make a test tool call…
troubleshoot.pullFailed: The download failed - check disk space and try again.
troubleshoot.serverFail: Nothing answers at {url} - start Ollama on this machine, or restart the stack with {cmd}.
troubleshoot.serverOk: The local model server answers at {url}.
troubleshoot.servingBlockedFix: Restart VegaDūta (in the install folder: scripts/vegaduta restart) - it repairs this on start. Or fix the entry under Platform Admin → LLM & Providers.
troubleshoot.servingBlockedPoolOff: But chats cannot use it: the platform model pool is switched off.
troubleshoot.servingBlockedRowDisabled: But chats cannot use it: its provider entry is disabled.
troubleshoot.servingBlockedRowUnusable: But chats cannot use it: its provider entry was saved under an earlier encryption key, or its address is blocked.
troubleshoot.sharedBody: This install does not run a local model, so there is nothing to diagnose here. On a shared or hosted install the model pools are managed by the platform operator - contact your admin; on your own install, deploy with local AI (scripts/vegaduta up --local-ai) and this page checks it.
troubleshoot.subtitle: Check the things an agentic turn needs on this install, and fix the common ones from here.
troubleshoot.title: Troubleshoot
troubleshoot.tooBig: Needs ~{ram} GB RAM free - this install is smaller than that
troubleshoot.toolsBody: Agents need the model to make tool calls (browse, run code, use skills). Run the test to confirm.
troubleshoot.useCreated: Registered this model server as the install's local provider, serving {tag}.
troubleshoot.useDisabled: {tag} is set on the local provider but that row is disabled - enable it under Platform Admin → LLM & Providers.
troubleshoot.useDone: Now serving {tag} - agents use it from the next turn.
troubleshoot.useFailed: Could not switch to {tag} - check that the model is still installed.
troubleshoot.useHint: Make agents use this model from the next turn - no restart needed

turnInspector.clientFailed: Recomputed in your browser: event {seq} fails ({reason}).
turnInspector.clientUnavailable: This browser cannot recompute hashes (no Web Crypto). Showing the server's verdict only.
turnInspector.clientVerified: Recomputed in your browser: all {count} hashes match.
turnInspector.disagree: The server and your browser disagree about the chain. Treat this journal as untrusted.
turnInspector.enableBody: Set app.turn-journal.enabled=true (environment variable APP_TURN_JOURNAL_ENABLED=true) on the core API and restart it. Turns that run afterwards are recorded; earlier turns cannot be recovered.
turnInspector.exportHint: Downloads JSON the Agent SDK testkit can load to replay this turn. Content stays redacted as returned.
turnInspector.forbiddenBody: Reading a turn journal needs the audit-log permission and viewer access to the agent.
turnInspector.idleBody: Enter the agent and turn IDs. Turn IDs are recorded for chat turns while the turn journal is on.
turnInspector.invalidIds: Agent ID and turn ID must both be UUIDs.
turnInspector.notFoundBody: Nothing was recorded for this turn. Either the IDs are wrong, or the turn journal was off when it ran. The journal is off by default and only records chat turns on the streaming fast path.
turnInspector.reasonCutOff: The answer was cut off at the length limit, so the model was asked to continue.
turnInspector.reasonFallbackProvider: The primary model failed, so the turn moved to the agent's fallback provider.
turnInspector.reasonGuardAction: A guardrail changed or withheld the answer.
turnInspector.reasonToolBlocked: A guard, policy, hook or limit answered instead of the tool, so it did not run.
turnInspector.reasonToolCallRetry: The model ended its answer with a malformed tool call, so it was asked again.
turnInspector.reasonToolParked: The call is waiting for a person to approve it; the tool has not run.
turnInspector.reasonToolsContinue: The model needed more steps after its tool calls, so the turn continued.
turnInspector.reasonToolsDisabledRetry: The provider refused the tool-call history, so the turn was answered once more without tools.
turnInspector.redactedNote: Payloads are never stored. Summaries are redacted; hashes prove content without revealing it.
turnInspector.sessEmptyBody: The session recorded nothing. Either the session ID is wrong, or the turn journal was off when its turns ran.
turnInspector.sessEmptyTitle: No journaled turns in this session
turnInspector.sessErrorTitle: Could not load the session's turns
turnInspector.sessInvalid: Enter the agent ID (a UUID) and the session ID.
turnInspector.sessSubtitle: Pick a chat session to see its recorded turns, newest first. Opening a chat message's view-turn link fills this in for you.
turnInspector.sessUnavailableBody: This server cannot list the turns of a session. Open a turn by its ID below instead.
turnInspector.subtitle: Replay what one agent turn did: intake, guardrails, model calls, tools, approvals, checks and the final commit, with a tamper-evident hash chain.
turnInspector.title: Turn inspector
turnInspector.tlApprovalAutoAllowed: {tool} ran without asking: a read-only call under Supervised
turnInspector.tlContentNote: Arguments and results are never stored. For a tool call the timeline shows its status, duration and the hashes of its arguments and result, not their content.
turnInspector.tlCopyFailed: Could not copy. Select the ID and copy it by hand.

workflowForms.waitDescription: Pause the run for a set time, until a date, or until an outside call resumes it. The pause is stored, so it survives restarts.
workflowForms.waitFeatureHint: Wait nodes only run when this deployment has them switched on; otherwise the workflow fails validation instead of skipping the wait.
workflowForms.waitModeWebhook: Until an outside call resumes it
workflowForms.waitTimeoutLabel: Give up after (hours, blank = the maximum)
workflowForms.waitUntilHint: An ISO 8601 date-time (a bare date means midnight UTC). Expressions from earlier nodes are allowed.
workflowForms.waitWebhookHint: The run gets a private resume link. Put {{$run.waitUrl}} in an earlier node (an email, an HTTP call, an agent message) to hand it to whoever should continue the run. Workflow editors can also read it from the run's wait details. POSTing JSON to it continues the run and the JSON becomes this node's output. The link works only while the run is parked at a Wait node.

workflowNode.errorPortTitle: On error - connect to a fallback node
workflowNode.fanOutOverWholeInput: Fans out over the whole input array
workflowNode.loopOverWholeInput: Loops over the whole input array
workflowNode.parallelFanOutHint: Fans out to every connected branch
workflowNode.voiceMenuNoMatchPortTitle: Caller pressed something that matches no option (after retries)

workflowNodesAi.aggregatorHint: Picks the first source that has a value. Each source is usually an earlier step's output, inserted as an expression.
workflowNodesAi.aggregatorLimitHint: A run follows one path, so this node does not wait for or merge branches. It reads the outputs of earlier steps by their label and picks the first with a value; a step that did not run counts as empty.
workflowNodesAi.classDescriptionPlaceholder: What belongs in this class, e.g. questions about invoices, refunds or payments
workflowNodesAi.classesHandleHint: The handle names the connection: renaming it disconnects any branch already drawn from that class. Use letters, digits and dashes.
workflowNodesAi.classifierHint: A model classifies the text at temperature 0. Its reply must name one of your classes exactly; anything else - an error, an unknown class, low confidence - sends the run to the default class. Draw one connection from each class port.
workflowNodesAi.documentHint: Reads a file or text and outputs plain text. PDF and Word files go through the same extractor as Knowledge uploads. The result is plain text, never run as anything.
workflowNodesAi.documentOutput_json: JSON with text, type, pages and whether it was cut
workflowNodesAi.documentSourceHint: An uploaded file's attachment key (chat-attachments/...), a web page URL, or the text itself. Web pages and text files can be read from a URL; PDF, Word and Excel files must be uploaded and passed by their attachment key.
workflowNodesAi.document_extractorDescription: Turns an uploaded PDF, Word, Excel, CSV, text, Markdown or HTML file (or a web page) into plain text, with size limits.
workflowNodesAi.extractorHint: A model reads the text and fills these parameters as strict JSON. It is told to answer null for anything the text does not state, and it never fills in a guess. An unusable reply is retried once.
workflowNodesAi.extractorOutputHint: The output is a JSON object with one key per parameter (null when the text does not state it) plus "_missing", the required parameters that could not be filled. Add a Condition node after this one to branch on _missing.
workflowNodesAi.instructionPlaceholder: e.g. Treat anything about a chargeback as billing
workflowNodesAi.limitsHint: Blank uses the workspace limits. A step can lower these limits but never raise them; anything past a limit is cut and the result says so.
workflowNodesAi.minConfidenceHint: If the model's confidence is below this, the run takes the default class instead. 0 turns the check off.
workflowNodesAi.modelOverrideHint: Only used when you bring your own provider key. Workspaces on the platform model always use the platform's model. Leave blank to use your active provider's default.
workflowNodesAi.paramDescriptionPlaceholder: What to look for in the text
workflowNodesAi.parameter_extractorDescription: Pulls named, typed values (text, number, yes/no, list, choice) out of free text. Values the text does not state stay empty, and missing required ones are reported.
workflowNodesAi.problem_badDefaultClass: The default class "{value}" is not one of the classes.
workflowNodesAi.problem_emptyHandle: A class has no handle - give every class a short name.
workflowNodesAi.problem_enumNoOptions: The choice parameter "{value}" needs at least one option.
workflowNodesAi.problem_handleTooLong: The handle "{value}..." is too long (64 characters at most).
workflowNodesAi.problem_invalidParamName: "{value}" is not a valid parameter name - start with a letter, then use letters, digits or underscores.
workflowNodesAi.problem_noParameters: Add at least one parameter to extract.
workflowNodesAi.problem_noSources: Add at least one source value.
workflowNodesAi.problem_reservedHandle: "{value}" is reserved for the failure port - choose another handle.
workflowNodesAi.problem_tooFewClasses: Add at least two classes so the node has something to choose between.
workflowNodesAi.question_classifierDescription: A model reads the text and picks exactly one of your classes, then the run follows that class's branch. Anything unclear goes to your default class.
workflowNodesAi.textHint: Leave blank to use this node's input. Earlier results can be inserted with {{ }} expressions.
workflowNodesAi.variable_aggregatorDescription: Takes the first of several earlier results that actually has a value. No model call.

workflowNodesData.aggregateDescription: Count, sum, average or combine a list, optionally grouped by a field.
workflowNodesData.aggregateHint: Without a group the result is one object; with a group it is a list with one object per group, in order of first appearance.
workflowNodesData.caseDuplicateWarn: Another case already has this name - names must be unique.
workflowNodesData.caseReservedWarn: This name is reserved - pick another.
workflowNodesData.dedupeByPlaceholder: id, email - blank compares whole items
workflowNodesData.dedupeDescription: Drop repeated items, comparing whole items or chosen fields.
workflowNodesData.dedupeHint: Compares the chosen fields (or whole items). Values of different types are different: 1 and "1" are not duplicates.
workflowNodesData.filterDescription: Keep only the items of a list that match your conditions.
workflowNodesData.filterHint: Numbers compare as numbers and ISO dates as dates; everything else compares as text. Items without the field never match greater/less comparisons.
workflowNodesData.groupByPlaceholder: a field, or several separated by commas
workflowNodesData.itemsFieldHint: Leave blank when the previous step's output is the list itself. If the list sits inside an object such as {"rows": [...]}, type its field name - the rest of the object is kept.
workflowNodesData.join_inner: Only rows found in every input
workflowNodesData.join_left: All rows of the first input
workflowNodesData.keepOnlySetLabel: Keep only the fields set here (drop everything else)
workflowNodesData.limitDescription: Keep only the first or last N items of a list.
workflowNodesData.limitHint: Keeps the first or last N items of the list. N may be an expression.
workflowNodesData.mergeDescription: Combine inputs: append them, join on a key, or take the first non-empty one.
workflowNodesData.mergeHint: Combines what reaches this step. After a Parallel, Fan-out or Loop step the input is a list with one entry per branch or item, and that is what gets merged. To combine named steps instead, add sources below. A run follows one path, so Merge cannot wait for branches that never ran - it combines what is present.
workflowNodesData.mergeMode_append: Append - put all inputs in one list
workflowNodesData.mergeMode_join: Join - match rows on a key
workflowNodesData.minInputsHint: If fewer inputs than this are present the step is skipped instead of producing a thin result. 0 means no minimum.
workflowNodesData.regexHint: Regex uses Java syntax. A pattern can be at most 200 characters, values longer than 10,000 characters are not tested, and every match has a short time limit.
workflowNodesData.setDescription: Add or change fields on the data. Values can use expressions.
workflowNodesData.setHint: Each field is written onto the data from the previous step. Values may use expressions such as {{ $json.total }}; they are worked out once for this step (put Set inside a Loop to compute per item).
workflowNodesData.setTypeHint: Auto turns numbers, true/false, null and JSON into real values; pick Text to keep something like 01234 exactly as written.
workflowNodesData.sortDescription: Order a list by one or more fields - numbers, dates or text.
workflowNodesData.sortHint: Stable: items that tie keep their order. Missing or empty values always sort last.
workflowNodesData.summaryMergeNoKey: Pick a key to join on
workflowNodesData.switchDescription: Send the run down one of several named paths by matching conditions.
workflowNodesData.switchHint: Cases are tested top to bottom and the first one that matches decides the path. Each case becomes an output port named after it; anything unmatched leaves through Default. Fields are read from the incoming data (a blank field tests the whole text).
